_source: Condensed from HPE's hosted Orchestrator MCP tool descriptions (Orchestrator 9.7.1.42046), reworded. Write notes only where HPE's read-side detail is about a schema or parameter the write shares.

notes.GET /acls: An unknown nePk gives 500 'Failed to load appliance data', never 404 or 400; that message also masks other post-fetch failures. For appliances older than 8.1.0.0 (or blank version) match criteria are rewritten to the current string-matching format. cached=true with no row gives 404 'may be unreachable', meaning never polled; retry cached=false, which writes the cache. Any live failure is 500 '<nePk>: Failed to get data from appliance.'
notes.GET /action: startTime/endTime must be epoch milliseconds; seconds returns zero rows. logLevel 0 also includes rows whose level is null. There is no more-available signal: exactly limit rows may mean older entries exist, so raise limit or narrow the window, appliance or username.
notes.GET /alarm/alarmConfig: Always a list; [] when never configured (Orchestrator then raises ALARM_EMAIL_NOT_SET until a rule is saved). On read, format defaults to 'HTML Formatted' when missing or blank. emailAddresses is one comma-separated string split on commas only: a semicolon makes one bad recipient and spaces after commas are kept. For RCA and Both rules the four severity booleans are ignored; they always notify on all four severities.
notes.GET /alarm/applianceSubAlarms: instanceId is the parent alarm's instanceId field, not its id or sequenceId (a wrong one returns []). [] only means no sub-alarms visible, not that the parent has none. Result is the appliance's own `outstanding` array. Live appliance call: unknown nePk is a generic 500; an out-of-range instanceId is a 404 HTML page.
notes.GET /alarm/correlatedAlarms: view accepts only active or closed (case-insensitive); 'all' gives 400, and a value outside the enum gives 500. severity is upper-cased the same unguarded way, so an invalid value also gives 500. HPE also names /alarm/correlatedRcAlarms for root-cause alarms only, which has no severity filter.
notes.GET /alarm/correlationSettings: Only two fields; remoteNotificationType is standard|correlated|both. With no stored rows the defaults are correlationEnabled false and remoteNotificationType correlated (Swagger says true; HPE reports false), indistinguishable from a saved setting. The aggregation row rewritten by the POST is not readable here.
notes.GET /alarm/correlationStatus: lastCorrelatedTime is computed live from current and historical correlated alarms and is 0 when none exist. lastRunTime is written by the correlation engine and stays 0 until the engine has run at least once, even while correlation is enabled.
notes.GET /alarm/count/appliance: The two reads cover different alarms, so totals differ: /alarm/summary unions Orchestrator and appliance alarms, /alarm/count/appliance is appliance-only. Only appliances with at least one open alarm appear in the counts; absent means zero and [] is a healthy fleet. Buckets are numOfCriticalAlarms, numOfMajorAlarms, numOfMinorAlarms, numOfWarningAlarms; summary has no total. With an API key the whole fleet is returned (AAG scoping skipped).
notes.GET /alarm/customization/severity: Nothing to return is 204 with no body, not {}: it means no override exists (or none for that alarmTypeId). Result is a map of alarm type id to uppercase WARNING, MINOR, MAJOR or CRITICAL. Only deviations from the built-in default are stored, so a type missing here runs at its default. With alarmTypeId the map has at most one entry.
notes.GET /alarm/delayEmail: Returns only {duration} in seconds (0-3600, enforced on write only); 204 with no body when no row exists, which acts the same as duration 0 (disabled). Active alarms are emailed only after lasting longer than duration; an alarm that raises and clears within the delay is never emailed at all (still visible in the alarm APIs). Global, not per appliance.
notes.GET /alarm/gms: view=active returns rows without cleared fields; closed and all add clearedTimeUtc, clearedTimeInMills and clearBy. Non-active views order by raised time, so maxAlarms silently keeps the most recently raised, not most recently cleared; default maxAlarms is 1000. severity is warning, minor, major or critical. A bad view, bad severity or out-of-range maxAlarms all give the same 400 'Request is invalid - supply correct input'.
notes.GET /alarm/notification: Payload is one boolean {"enable": true}, default true. The first call with no stored row inserts the default row, so this GET writes. Disabling it also suppresses portal broadcast emails, and enable true alone does not prove mail is sent (an alarm-email config row must exist). A corrupt row gives 500 text/html 'Error retrieving alarm notification'.
notes.GET /alarm/summary: The two reads cover different alarms, so totals differ: /alarm/summary unions Orchestrator and appliance alarms, /alarm/count/appliance is appliance-only. Only appliances with at least one open alarm appear in the counts; absent means zero and [] is a healthy fleet. Buckets are numOfCriticalAlarms, numOfMajorAlarms, numOfMinorAlarms, numOfWarningAlarms; summary has no total. With an API key the whole fleet is returned (AAG scoping skipped).
notes.GET /alarm/suppress: Two independent axes: {alarmTypeIds, applianceIds}. An applianceIds entry silences every alarm from that appliance regardless of type. Both keys are always present (empty lists when unused) and the call is always 200. It reads an in-memory cache loaded at startup, so direct DB edits are invisible until restart. Air-gap mode adds fixed portal/registration alarm type ids to the cache. Ids are alarm type ids, not alarm instances.
notes.GET /apiKey: key is always empty (the value is shown only at creation) and ipList is always null. The allow-list is in whitelist, a JSON-encoded string where '[]' or 'null' means no restriction. active is a stored flag never updated on expiry; judge by expiration (Unix seconds, 0 = never). HPE warns the name filter blanks the cached key so that key gets 403 until restart; filter the full list instead.
notes.GET /appliance: state is an integer: 0 unknown, 1 normal (reachable), 2 unreachable, 3 unsupported version, 4 out of sync, 5 sync in progress, 6 partial connectivity, 7 connected, 8 not connected. There is no reachability string field. This is where nePk values come from.
notes.GET /appliance/adminDistance: cached=true reads only the Orchestrator cache: no row gives 404 'not found in the database' (retry cached=false); a row with null data gives 200 with an empty body, meaning no data, not no distances. cached=false goes live and writes the cache. 404 'not supported for appliance' means the appliance lacks the endpoint, do not retry. Unknown nePk is 400 'Appliance nePk is invalid.'
notes.GET /appliance/approved: All three endpoints are ETag-cached. queuedForDeletion lists appliances whose removal is in flight.
notes.GET /appliance/backup: Each backup record's key is id, not backupFilePk; a restore request body wants backupFilePk set to that record's id.
notes.GET /appliance/cpustat/historical/isfetc: Fetch state is global: only one fetch job exists per Orchestrator, so isfetchinprogress validates nePk then ignores it and describes whichever appliance's fetch is running. GET /appliance/cpustat/historical/maxtimestamp?nePk is the per-appliance one and returns epoch ms, showing how current the pulled CPU history is.
notes.GET /appliance/customTagMeta: These read the Orchestrator cache, not the appliance. Omit nePk for the whole-fleet map. ETag-cached, so a matching If-None-Match gives 304. customTagMeta is an empty list for an appliance with no tags.
notes.GET /appliance/denied: All three endpoints are ETag-cached. queuedForDeletion lists appliances whose removal is in flight.
notes.GET /appliance/discovered: Also triggers a discovery refresh. serial, hostname, model, softwareVersion and ip are nested under applianceInfo, not top level (top level reads null).
notes.GET /appliance/extraInfo: This GET writes: if the appliance has no stored extraInfo row, one is inserted. extraInfo then holds location, contact and overlaySettings as null (a non-empty object, identical to a saved empty record). location has address, address2, city, state, zipCode, country but no latitude or longitude. Unknown nePk is 404 'Invalid nePk'; missing nePk is 400.
notes.GET /appliance/haPeerMeta: These read the Orchestrator cache, not the appliance. Omit nePk for the whole-fleet map. ETag-cached, so a matching If-None-Match gives 304. customTagMeta is an empty list for an appliance with no tags.
notes.GET /appliance/interfaceMeta: These read the Orchestrator cache, not the appliance. Omit nePk for the whole-fleet map. ETag-cached, so a matching If-None-Match gives 304. customTagMeta is an empty list for an appliance with no tags.
notes.GET /appliance/networkRoleAndSite: Returns the whole appliance record (about 39 keys), not just networkRole and site. password is always null; id equals nePk and IP equals ip; preconfigStatus is always null here, so read it elsewhere. An nePk unknown to Orchestrator gives a generic 500 'There was an internal server error.', not a 404; check it against GET /appliance.
notes.GET /appliance/peerPriorityList: Shape depends on appliance version: 8.3.3 and later (except 9.0.x below 9.0.2) nest peers under peerlist with peer_weight and peer_metric; older releases give a flat peer map with peer_weight only, so missing peer_metric means older software. cached is true only when absent or exactly 'true'. A cached 404 after an upgrade across that boundary is normal; cached=false refills the cache.
notes.GET /appliance/pppoeList: cached=true with no stored row is a 404 meaning never polled, not unsupported; retry cached=false to seed it. cached=false needs deploymentMode router (otherwise 500 "Not available in current mode."), overwrites the cache, and an appliance 404 stores an unavailable marker that makes later cached=true reads report unavailable. Blank nePk is 400 "Invalid nePk"; unknown nePk is 400 "Appliance nePk is invalid."
notes.GET /appliance/queuedForDeletion: All three endpoints are ETag-cached. queuedForDeletion lists appliances whose removal is in flight.
notes.GET /appliance/rest: Appliance passthrough: url is the appliance's own REST path (e.g. memory, sysLimits, networkRoutes) and the answer comes live from the appliance. A 404 or an empty result often means the appliance lacks the feature, hardware or software release (PoE, power supply on a virtual appliance, older builds), not a bad request. Counters such as flow and IDS stats are cumulative since boot; poll twice and use deltas.
notes.GET /appliance/scalars: Returns the appliance's flat single-value config knobs. cached defaults true (Orchestrator cache); false is live. Blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /appliance/shell/shellAccessSetting: Per-appliance setting forwarded to the appliance's own /shell/shellAccessSetting, from which the `password` field is extracted; distinct from the Orchestrator-wide /shell/shellAccessSetting. Blank nePk is 400 INVALID_NEPK.
notes.GET /appliance/statsConfig: GET /appliance/statsConfig/default returns the built-in defaults instead of the current fabric-wide config.
notes.GET /appliance/zoneListMeta: These read the Orchestrator cache, not the appliance. Omit nePk for the whole-fleet map. ETag-cached, so a matching If-None-Match gives 304. customTagMeta is an empty list for an appliance with no tags.
notes.GET /appliancesSoftwareVersions: GET cached 404 'Failed to get data from GMS Cache' means not polled yet; use cached=false (on connection failure it returns 200 with the text 'REST API call to /appliancesSoftwareVersions failed!'). POST /validateApplianceUpgrade takes {nePks}, needs READ_WRITE, silently drops unknown nePks (all unknown validates every appliance), and returns a sentence in Air-Gap mode; errors usually come from the Cloud Portal.
notes.GET /application/userDefinedConfig: Returns the user-app config actually on that appliance, not the Orchestrator-wide catalog. Cached with no stored NeConfig is 404 "may be unreachable" (a cache miss); cached=false pulls live and refreshes the cache.
notes.GET /applicationDefinition: A generic key-value store, not a dump: base is required and resourceKey picks one row. base=/applicationTags with resourceKey=merged is the full app-group set (MBs); /applications with hashcode is a small fingerprint. A miss, or a match on more than one row, is 200 {"result":"Not found"}. An empty resourceKey looks up the NULL-key row. A leading slash on base is optional.
notes.GET /applicationDefinition/appExpressApp: Swagger marks resourceKey required (userDefined or merged); HPE describes it as optional, omitted for all configs or set to a specific app config key.
notes.GET /applicationDefinition/appExpressGro: Flat list of {nePk, appExpressGroupName}, one row per pair; nothing stored is an empty list. The groupName filter is case-sensitive though writes lowercase the key: "Retail" 404s, "retail" matches (404 only when other associations exist). This read is not scoped to your Appliance Access Group, but the write is, so posting the read back from a scoped key deletes associations outside your scope.

Returns a map keyed by the lowercased group name (a group created as 'Retail' is keyed retail), not a list. {} is ambiguous: it means no groups configured or a stored blob that failed to parse (the error is only logged). Never a 404.
notes.GET /applicationDefinition/ipIntelligenc: Result is a map keyed by name of {name, priority}. A named read returns the entry only when more than one override is stored; otherwise it is 200 with {} even though the override exists. A whitespace name such as a single space returns the whole map (handler accident).
notes.GET /applicationGroups: A cached read with no cached row for the appliance is 404 "No application groups configured." (not an empty body); cached=false fetches live and refreshes the cache.
notes.GET /applicationTrends: traffic: OPTIMIZED_TRAFFIC, PASS_THROUGH_SHAPED, PASS_THROUGH_UNSHAPED or ALL_TRAFFIC (case-insensitive); bound: INBOUND or OUTBOUND. Empty traffic or bound gives 400 "... parameter is mandatory". HPE reports 500 on environments that have not accumulated application-trends stats yet.
notes.GET /autoTunedProperties: Flat object of five integers with inconsistent casing: threadPoolSize, ParallelOrchestrationTasks, ParallelActionTasks, ParallelReachabilityTasks, jettyMaxThreads. These are live applied values that never decrease, so large numbers do not mean a large fleet now. The tuple 1000/50/100/20/600 is both the table value for 200 or fewer appliances and the fallback if the tuner failed, so it is ambiguous.
notes.GET /avcMode: Without nePk it returns the fleet rollup {"AVC": "none"|"all"|"mixed"}, based on how many appliances run a version with the new AVC engine. With nePk it returns that appliance's mode {"AVC": "old"|"new"}.
notes.GET /banners: cached=true returns 404 (not an empty body) when no banner row is cached for the appliance; use cached=false to fetch live and refresh the cache.
notes.GET /bgp/config/allVrfs/neighbor: Result is keyed per VRF segment, unlike the default-VRF BGP reads. Intended for appliances running BGP inside multiple segments.
notes.GET /bgp/config/allVrfs/system: Result is keyed per VRF segment, unlike the default-VRF BGP reads. Intended for appliances running BGP inside multiple segments.
notes.GET /brandCustomization: No role is required beyond an authenticated key. Never customized gives 204 with an empty body, not {}. The map is keyed by type (footer, welcomeText, patentText, orchText, supportLinkURL, homePageTitle) to {useDefault, custom}; a type using the default is absent, not listed with useDefault=true.
notes.GET /brandCustomization/image: Returns a map of image type to {fileName}; only slots with an upload appear, so a missing key means that slot uses the default. With no custom images the answer is 204 with an empty body, not {}. Types: bannerImage, favicon, backgroundImage, logoImage, treeImage. No role is required.
notes.GET /bridgeGroups: cached=true with no stored row is 404 "could not be found. It may be unreachable", which means never polled, not a bad nePk; there is no live fallback, so retry cached=false. {"available":false} style 404 means feature absent. Live path: software older than 9.0.3.0 gives 500 "Unsupported Version", and an appliance 404 stores a not-available marker that makes later cached reads 404. Live reads write the cache.
notes.GET /cache/syncState: Entries have resourcePath, databaseData, cachedData, syncRequired. A null side means read failure or not configured, indistinguishable, and one null makes syncRequired true. Objects are compared from the DB side only, so extra cache keys are not flagged. Secrets are masked: six asterisks on cachedData is in sync, three means out of sync. Covers only a fixed internal set; the HPE SSE appliance-association entry is always inert.
notes.GET /cache/userApps: Returns a map of application to the appliances (NEInfo) that have it. GET /cache/userApps is the user-defined cache; GET /cache/builtinApps is the built-in one. Useful for diagnosing application-classification cache state.
notes.GET /cloudDeployment/aws/accounts: Secrets come back as empty strings (AWS secretKey, Azure clientSecret, GCP key); non-secret ids stay in clear. AWS and Azure accounts have a UUID id; GCP has none and is keyed by project. Empty AWS/Azure accounts means none configured, but an empty GCP list is ambiguous because a parse failure is swallowed there. secretKey is always blanked. An unknown id returns 204 with an empty body, not 404. For GCP the id is the project id.
notes.GET /cloudDeployment/aws/edgeconnects: Secrets come back as empty strings (AWS secretKey, Azure clientSecret, GCP key); non-secret ids stay in clear. AWS and Azure accounts have a UUID id; GCP has none and is keyed by project. Empty AWS/Azure accounts means none configured, but an empty GCP list is ambiguous because a parse failure is swallowed there.
notes.GET /cloudDeployment/aws/edgeconnects/cl: id is the Orchestrator deployment id and defaults to -1 server-side, so always pass it. Returns the actual cloud objects the deployment created (VPC/VNet, subnets, instances, IPs).
notes.GET /cloudDeployment/aws/edgeconnects/de: Numeric status: 0 NOT_STARTED, 1 PENDING, 2 DEPLOYING, 3 SUCCESS, 4 INCOMPLETE, 5 DESTROYING. 4 is a partial deploy, not 'failed'; there is no failed code. 2 and 5 mean in flight.
notes.GET /cloudDeployment/aws/edgeconnects/lo: Each provider/service path has its own /log (Azure has edgeconnects, azure-nva, route-server and load-balancer variants). id is the Orchestrator deployment id and defaults to -1 server-side when omitted.
notes.GET /cloudDeployment/azure-nva/edgeconne: Secrets come back as empty strings (AWS secretKey, Azure clientSecret, GCP key); non-secret ids stay in clear. AWS and Azure accounts have a UUID id; GCP has none and is keyed by project. Empty AWS/Azure accounts means none configured, but an empty GCP list is ambiguous because a parse failure is swallowed there. With id, a 404 means it is not an azure_nva deployment id. Omitting id returns all azure_nva deployments, and an empty list if there are none.
