notes.GET /cluster: GET /cluster is the runtime state (member roles and health); GET /cluster/alarmCount is the current cluster-alarm count. The configured profiles are at /cluster/profiles.
notes.GET /cluster/alarmCount: GET /cluster is the runtime state (member roles and health); GET /cluster/alarmCount is the current cluster-alarm count. The configured profiles are at /cluster/profiles.
notes.GET /cluster/profileMapping: On an Orchestrator where nothing is configured yet, both /cluster/profiles and /cluster/profileMapping answer 400 'There was an error when reading cluster profile ...'; that is a false alarm, not a fault (a corrupt row gives the same 400 on profiles). Profile keys are omitted when never set. The mapping is an object keyed by profile id with unordered appliance keys.
notes.GET /cluster/profiles: On an Orchestrator where nothing is configured yet, both /cluster/profiles and /cluster/profileMapping answer 400 'There was an error when reading cluster profile ...'; that is a false alarm, not a fault (a corrupt row gives the same 400 on profiles). Profile keys are omitted when never set. The mapping is an object keyed by profile id with unordered appliance keys.
notes.GET /configReportDisk: Reports disk hardware, not free space. An unreachable appliance is not an error: you get 200 with the string 'REST API call to /configReportDisk/<nePk> failed!' instead of an object. Unknown nePk is 500. Success is {id, disks}, with disks keyed by slot index; size is GB, pair -1 means unpaired, and a drive is failing when smart value reaches thold_val. Each call also refreshes the Orchestrator's cache.
notes.GET /configurationLimit: Returns the appliance's stored scalars as a flat object (e.g. maxFlows, maxAclrulelen, supportsBypass, isPortalLicensed); it is read from the Orchestrator database only and never contacts the appliance. 404 "Appliance with key ... may be unreachable" means no scalars were ever polled (or unknown id), not that it is down. Blank nePk is 400 "Invalid nePk". Role needs the DEBUG menu.
notes.GET /customApplianceTags: cached=false also overwrites the Orchestrator's cached copy, so it is a write. Tags are keyed by tag ID with nested {name, value}, not name to value. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" only means nothing is cached yet; retry cached=false. 204 with no body is a cached row with no data, distinct from {} (no tags). Unknown nePk: 404 cached, generic 500 live.
notes.GET /customCert: Response is a list of certificates; key is the full decrypted PEM. createdTimestamp is epoch ms but lastUpdatedTimestamp is epoch seconds; expiration is ms. No valid flag: health is expirationStatus (Valid, Expiring soon under 60 days, Expired; daysToExpiration is -1 once expired). applianceSyncStatus int: 0 Deployed, 1 Deployment_pending, 2 Withdrawn, 3 Withdrawal_pending. One unparseable cert makes the whole list 500.
notes.GET /customCert/caCertsFromDefaultTrustS: Fetched live from the cloud portal, so it needs portal connectivity. Returns the default trusted CAs (parsed with issuer and subject), not the user-added custom certificates.
notes.GET /customCert/settings: Returns only autoSync and isRestartRequired (either can be null), not whether custom certs are enabled (that is GET /customCert/enable). isRestartRequired=true means the stored trust store differs from the one on disk; until Orchestrator restarts, no certificate changes are pushed to appliances. Values reflect stored intent, not the live TLS keystore.
notes.GET /dbPartition/info: Both filters are optional. GET /dbPartition/statsInfo is a fixed overview of the stats-table partitions and takes no parameters. Used to inspect stats DB partition sizes before pruning.
notes.GET /debugFiles: debugFiles "" at HTTP 200 means no files, an unknown nePk, or an unreachable appliance (indistinguishable); only blank nePk is a 400. Object is keyed by file type, absent when empty. Each stats has size in bytes and mtimeMs (epoch ms) on newer releases or mtime on older. debugDump names containing "tunbug" are returned though the UI hides them.
notes.GET /deployment: cached=true reads the database and returns an arbitrary first row; with no stored row it is 500 "Unable to find NE with PK <nePk>", not 404. cached=false goes live and any transport failure is 500 "Internal error while fetching deployment info", so 500 means stale or unreachable. A blank nePk, or one not yet loaded in the appliance cache, is 400 "Invalid nePk". An unparseable cached value means live.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig: On /dhcpConfig/reservations, source is an ordinal: 0 means appliance-created and 1 Orchestrator-created (not the declared 1 and 2). Copy it unchanged when posting back; writing 2 fails the whole list. An empty reservations list does not prove none are held: it is [] whenever no DHCP pool block is configured.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/dhcpSettings: Per-appliance DHCP config; nePk is required. If cached=true returns empty, the server retries live automatically. The bare /dhcpConfig endpoint is Orchestrator-wide and ignores nePk.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/leases: maxLease is a hard cap with silent truncation and no total; if the returned count equals maxLease, raise it or narrow with ip/mac. The UI caps at 10000.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/profiler: Despite the name this is the pair of DHCP relay helper addresses, shaped {ipHelper1,ipHelper2}. An unconfigured helper is not absent: it is ipAddress 0.0.0.0, segment 'Default', vrfId '0'. cached=true falls back to a live read when the cache is empty (hiding the cache-miss 404) and writes the result into the cache. If both are empty you get 200 with a zero-byte body.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/relay: cached=true silently falls back to a live read when the cache is missing or empty, and live reads overwrite the cache. With cached=false an appliance 404 is swallowed into 200 with an empty body (relay None), meaning the appliance refused, not that no relay is configured. Payload is the appliance /dhcpd/relay JSON, untouched.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/remoteSubnets: Reads the appliance's DHCP address pools, not relay subnets. cached=true silently falls back to a live read (and refills the cache) if the cache is missing or empty. cached=false on an appliance that lacks the resource returns 200 with an empty body, indistinguishable from no data. cached must be lowercase true/false; other spellings take the live path.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/reservation: Generic 500 "There was an internal server error." means unknown nePk. "<nePk>: Failed to get data from appliance." is 404 when the appliance returned 404 and 500 when it errored; bodies are identical, so read the status. A cached read with no row retries live automatically, so no cache-miss error appears.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/reservations: On /dhcpConfig/reservations, source is an ordinal: 0 means appliance-created and 1 Orchestrator-created (not the declared 1 and 2). Copy it unchanged when posting back; writing 2 fails the whole list. An empty reservations list does not prove none are held: it is [] whenever no DHCP pool block is configured.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/scope: Returns a top-level array of scopes with scopeName, subnet, type, total, allocated, available and utilization (percent). An appliance with no scopes returns an empty array, which is normal. cached=true falls back to a live read when the cache is empty and writes the result back; if both are empty you get 200 with a zero-byte body. UI offers it for 9.7.0.0_0000+.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/service: Returns {serverStatus, relayStatus}: two independent daemons. Both null or absent means DHCP was never configured, not down. Even cached=true goes live when the cache is empty (always for unconfigured appliances) and writes the live result back to the cache. A 404 here is real evidence the appliance did not answer; an unknown nePk gives a bare 500; if both paths are empty you get 200 with a zero-byte body. UI offers it for 9.7.0.0_0000+.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/state/failover: Response is a map keyed by opaque pair index; values hold failoverstate, mystate, partnerstate, mytime/partnertime (epoch seconds) and mclt (string). Empty map means no failover configured, not an error. Even cached=true silently falls back to a live fetch when the cache is empty, and any live fetch writes the cache. Unknown nePk gives a bare 500; if both paths are empty the result is 200 with a zero-byte body.
notes.GET /dhcpConfig/utilizationThreshold: Returns {scopeUtilizationThreshold: percent}, one threshold for all scopes. An absent key means never set (the UI shows 90 as a default; the API does not return it). cached=true silently falls back to a live read when the cache is empty, and a live read refills the cache. If both are empty the answer is 200 with an empty body. The UI offers it only for 9.7.0.0_0000 and later.
notes.GET /dnatMaps: Same data as GET /vrfSegments (shared cache row of /vrf/config/maps, byte-identical); cached=false here overwrites what a cached read of either returns. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" only means nothing cached yet; retry cached=false. Unknown nePk is an opaque 500.
notes.GET /dnsProxy/config: cached is tested as exact 'true' (default true only when absent); other spellings go live, and a live fetch writes the cache. The cache-miss 404 'may be unreachable' is just an empty cache; retry cached=false. /resolver and /dnsProxy/config are cached independently, so one can 404 while the other returns data. /resolver live failures are always 500, even for an unknown nePk. Error bodies are text/html.
notes.GET /exception/tunnel: No paging or nePk filter; it returns every exception. The wildcard is the lowercase string 'any'; apply-time matching is exact and case-sensitive, so 'ANY' passes validation but never matches. Matching is symmetric (1<->2 swapped). appliance_id_* is an nePk and interface_label_* a label id, not a name. Rows vanish when their appliance or label is deleted. Exceptions only stop tunnel build at the next overlay apply; existing tunnels stay.
notes.GET /fastWsFailover/lastMessageReceived: lastMessageReceived is {nePk:{wsSessionId:epochMs}} per websocket session; the earliest session timestamp is what counts. failoverModeOnAppliance is {nePk:mode-id} as echoed by the appliance, which can lag the Orchestrator-side mode after a change. Both maps are in-memory: a missing nePk means no live websocket, and both are empty after an Orchestrator restart.
notes.GET /fastWsFailover/mode/active: Times are milliseconds and all fields are -1 when disabled. wsFailoverMode is a mode id (e.g. "c"); GET /fastWsFailover/mode returns all modes keyed by id with no marker for which is active.
notes.GET /fastWsFailover/portalRedirection: Returns {nePk:{redirectedAt,lastPingReceived,consecutivePingCount}} in epoch ms. {} is the healthy state, not a failure. An absent nePk does not mean fine (entries also drop when its websocket closes), and entries self-clear after enough consecutive pings. In-memory only, empty after an Orchestrator restart.
notes.GET /flow: Rows in flows.flows are positional: [0]=flowId, [1]=flowSeq. Query params go straight to the appliance, so filter is not a fixed enum ('all' is safe; appliance trafficType codes are 1 all, 2 optimized, 3 passthrough, 4 passthrough-unshaped). Send bytes (UI uses last5m; 'total' is widest). To find a host as source or destination set ip2=ip1 and ipEitherFlag=true. Results truncate silently at maxFlows.
notes.GET /flow/flowBandwidthStats: Get id and seq from the active-flow search (id is element 0, seq element 1 of each flow row). flowBandwidthStats and flowOptimization are best-effort; flowOptimization takes only nePk (it is not per-flow). Requires the same nePk, id and seq for flowDetails2 and flowBandwidthStats.
notes.GET /flow/flowDetails2: Get id and seq from the active-flow search (id is element 0, seq element 1 of each flow row). flowBandwidthStats and flowOptimization are best-effort; flowOptimization takes only nePk (it is not per-flow). Requires the same nePk, id and seq for flowDetails2 and flowBandwidthStats.
notes.GET /flow/flowOptimization: Get id and seq from the active-flow search (id is element 0, seq element 1 of each flow row). flowBandwidthStats and flowOptimization are best-effort; flowOptimization takes only nePk (it is not per-flow). Requires the same nePk, id and seq for flowDetails2 and flowBandwidthStats.
notes.GET /gms/advancedProperties: GET /gms/advancedProperties/metadata lists each property's default and constraints; read it for valid keys and values before changing a property.
notes.GET /gms/appliance/preconfiguration: Response shape depends on params: none returns all with configData base64; filter=names returns names only (no ids); filter=metadata returns one row per preconfig without configData; preconfigId returns one, and an unknown id is 404 "Preconfig not found." as text. filter and preconfigId must not be combined (400). The /default form ignores both and returns configData null if the template file is missing.
notes.GET /gms/appliance/preconfiguration/appl: nePk is required (400 if blank) and an unknown nePk is 404. The site value comes from the appliance's /spPortal/config registration data.
notes.GET /gms/applianceWizard/apply: Returns only {actionGroupId}; poll GET /action/status?key=<id> for detail. An empty id means no wizard ran, it finished, or the nePk does not exist (always 200, nePk not validated). A non-empty id also covers queued-not-started and an apply interrupted by a restart, which stays in progress forever. A failed step still completes, so inspect per-step results.
notes.GET /gms/backup: password is always returned as "" (never the stored secret). Fields: protocol (an int code), hostname, username, directory, port, maxBackups. 404 means no backup config exists yet.
notes.GET /gms/backup/exportTemplate: mode is TEMPLATE or MIGRATION. TEMPLATE is rejected with 400 if the Orchestrator manages any appliances or has any Cloud Services configured. MIGRATION is blocked with 500 when apply-overlay is enabled or IKEless seed rotation is an enabled scheduled job. Read-only; download=true requests the file form.
notes.GET /gms/discovery: Holds only notification emails ({emails, secondaryAccounts}); nothing about how discovery works. This GET can write: with no row (or emails null) it pulls portal-registration emails and saves them. 404 means no config and the Orchestrator is not registered with the portal (or no portal emails), not merely unset. secondaryAccounts is back-filled from portal registration and can be {}.
notes.GET /gms/dynamicTopologyConfig: Per-user: keyed by the session user, not a query param. A user with no saved config gets 404 "Dynamic Topology config not found."
notes.GET /gms/gmsRegistration2: Without nePk it returns the global info {customDefaultIP, internalManagementIP, label priority map} with the legacy defaultIPOrDns nulled. With nePk it returns the specific Orchestrator IP/FQDN that one appliance would use, or an error string if that resolution fails.
notes.GET /gms/grNode: Omitting grNodePk lists all nodes, but the result is RBAC-filtered to the caller's assigned assets unless the request is local/API-key or the user has no asset restriction. Nodes carry wx/wy (map pixel coords) and latitude/longitude.
notes.GET /gms/group: Each group is {id, name, subType, parentId}. subType 0=ROOT, 1=GMS, 2=AUTO_DISCOVERED, 3=REGULAR; only REGULAR groups can be renamed or deleted (400 otherwise). API-key calls always receive every group, not an RBAC-filtered subset.
notes.GET /gms/group/root: Returns the root group; its id is the parent for top-level groups. It is a system group (subType 0, ROOT) and cannot be renamed or deleted.
notes.GET /gms/interfaceLabels: With type set, the backend returns only that side's list (not the {lan, wan} object) and answers 404 'No interface labels found for <side>' when that side is empty instead of []. Omit type to get both sides as an object, which is empty-safe. An invalid type is 400; the check is case-insensitive.
notes.GET /gms/internalSubnets2: Returns the whole config {ipv4, ipv6, segmentIpv4, segmentIpv6 ("<segment>:<subnet>"), segmentedIpv6Enabled, nonDefaultRoutes}. A never-configured Orchestrator returns defaults (empty lists, segmentedIpv6Enabled true, nonDefaultRoutes false), not a 404. The legacy /gms/internalSubnets returns only {"subnets":[...]} (ipv4 only); never post that shape back, because the write replaces everything.
notes.GET /gms/ipAllowList/drops: Rows are {ip, resource, xForwardedFor, lastContact}, newest first; resource is the request URI and lastContact is epoch milliseconds. An hourly job keeps only the newest 1000 rows, so a broad lockout can push older evidence out. A row is also written when an API-key request fails that key's own allow-list.
notes.GET /gms/ipAllowList/external: Entries are {subnet, comment}. External is the master switch: when empty, every source IP is admitted and the internal list is never consulted. The lists gate only requests without an API key; X-AUTH-TOKEN calls are checked against that key's own allow-list.
notes.GET /gms/ipAllowList/useSocketIP: HPE says the result is a bare true/false. true means the allow list is checked against the TCP peer (nginx X-Real-IP, else socket address); false uses the trusted-proxy-validated client IP from forwarding headers. Unlike other allow-list GETs this one needs net_read_write: a read-only key gets 403.
notes.GET /gms/job: prevFireTime 0 means never run or the lookup failed. schedule, cron and config arrive as embedded JSON objects. /gms/job/historical is capped at 10000 rows ordered by end time ascending, so a busy Orchestrator returns the oldest runs, not the latest. In historical, status 1 started, 2 success, 3 failed (detail in statusText), assocId is the job id (0 if unscheduled), times are epoch ms.
notes.GET /gms/job/debug: Raw Quartz JobDebug list (trigger state, next/previous fire times, misfire info): a scheduler troubleshooting view, deeper than the configured-jobs listing.
notes.GET /gms/job/historical: Capped at 10000 rows ordered by end time ascending, so a busy Orchestrator returns the oldest runs, not the latest. status 1 started, 2 success, 3 failed (detail in statusText); assocId is the scheduled job id (0 if unscheduled); times are epoch ms.
notes.GET /gms/job/reportViewport: No UI sets this, so 404 with plain-text body 'Not found.' is the normal never-configured state (defaults apply), not a fault. Stored JSON is {"<tab display name>": {width,height}}; keys must be display names (Health Map, Loss, Jitter Trends, Top Talkers, matched case-insensitively), not tab ids, or they are silently ignored. Tabs not listed, or 0/0, use the built-in size.
notes.GET /gms/overlays/association: Response is a map {"<overlayId>": [nePk, ...]}. Inverted codes: 400 "Invalid overlay ID passed, overlay does not exist" means no such overlay; 404 "Not found." means the overlay exists but has no readable members, or the stored record is missing (indistinguishable). A corrupt stored record is 500 "Internal error while retreiving associations for overlay".
notes.GET /gms/overlays/config: Without overlayId the list comes from an in-memory cache that can lag the database, and one unparseable row silently drops itself and all later rows (still 200). With overlayId the read is authoritative and returns a one-element list. Only global (region 0) rows are returned. 404 means no such overlay or a non-numeric overlayId (the body text says which); 500 'Not able to parse overlay config' means a corrupt stored row.
notes.GET /gms/overlays/config/regions: Send both overlayId and regionId, or neither; sending only one gives 400 'overlayId or regionId is missing.' Omitting both returns every regional config as a nested map.
notes.GET /gms/permissions: Swagger says the result is rw or r; HPE reports a {feature: permission} map for the effective feature permissions of the user.
notes.GET /gms/scheduleTimezone: Returns {"scheduleTimezone":{"defaultTimezone":tz}}, the timezone in which scheduled-job times are interpreted. With no stored config it returns the Orchestrator host's own default timezone as if it were a setting, so a value does not prove it was configured. Supports If-None-Match (304).
notes.GET /gms/services: Both reads return maps keyed by service id (service_<N> user-defined; sp_zscaler, sp_netskope, sp_axis, sp_service<N> third-party), sharing one id namespace. Null fields are omitted, so entries may lack id. A missing config is an empty map at 200; {} from /gms/services is normal on a fresh Orchestrator. On /gms/thirdPartyServices, enabled is computed at read time from subscriptions, not an admin toggle.
notes.GET /gms/sessionTimeout: Body is wrapped as {"sessionSettings": <config row>} whose configData is {autoLogout, maxSession}. autoLogout is the idle timeout in minutes (default 30); maxSession is the maximum concurrent UI sessions (default 20).
notes.GET /gms/stats/approximateDiskSpace: Values are bytes per minute, not a total; multiply by retention seconds / collection interval. Omitting applianceCount gives a 500. numberOfTunnels, if omitted, comes from live counts using integer division (reads low); tunnel stats then ignore applianceCount. numberOfOverlays is ignored. numberOfSegments (1-24) affects only DDoS stats. Disabled stats are still estimated.
notes.GET /gms/stats/collection: Flat map of statType to bool. A stat type absent from the map is treated as disabled by the collector, so absence is meaningful. Disabling a type stops the Orchestrator storing that table (charts and history lost); the flag reaches appliances through the periodic stats-collector push, not immediately.
notes.GET /gms/stats/retention: Map keyed by stat name to a list of {retention, granularity}; no statType or partitionDuration field (the map key is the statType). granularity is uppercase (MINUTE). Incomplete by design: loss, latency, appliancememory, health and applianceprocessstate are always excluded and application/flowapp depend on AVC mode, so a missing stat is not proof it has no retention.
notes.GET /gms/stats/statsRetentionNotificatio: Returns the stored config text verbatim, or the literal string {} when nothing was saved; it never 404s. It records whether a user dismissed the stats-retention/disk-threshold banner.
notes.GET /gms/statsCollection: The bare GET has a side effect: if the config row is absent (normal), it writes a fresh all-true row, so 'current' is a default just saved. That row is replayed at every database upgrade and can re-enable stat types you disabled. The live toggles are at /gms/stats/collection; prefer them. GET /gms/statsCollection/default is a pure read.
notes.GET /gms/statsCollection/default: The bare GET has a side effect: if the config row is absent (normal), it writes a fresh all-true row, so 'current' is a default just saved. That row is replayed at every database upgrade and can re-enable stat types you disabled. The live toggles are at /gms/stats/collection; prefer them. GET /gms/statsCollection/default is a pure read.
notes.GET /gms/thirdPartyServices: Both reads return maps keyed by service id (service_<N> user-defined; sp_zscaler, sp_netskope, sp_axis, sp_service<N> third-party), sharing one id namespace. Null fields are omitted, so entries may lack id. A missing config is an empty map at 200; {} from /gms/services is normal on a fresh Orchestrator. On /gms/thirdPartyServices, enabled is computed at read time from subscriptions, not an admin toggle.
notes.GET /gms/topologyConfig: topologyConfig is per caller (the API key's name), and an unsaved config is returned as a copy of the site default, not an error. linkInfo needs overlayId (blank is 400) and returns an N x N matrix indexed by nePks position: 0 no tunnel, 1 up, 2 partially down, 3 down, 4 no status. linkInfo is null (still 200) at 1000+ appliances by default, and an unknown overlayId gives an all-zero matrix.
notes.GET /gms/topologyConfig/linkInfo: topologyConfig is per caller (the API key's name), and an unsaved config is returned as a copy of the site default, not an error. linkInfo needs overlayId (blank is 400) and returns an N x N matrix indexed by nePks position: 0 no tunnel, 1 up, 2 partially down, 3 down, 4 no status. linkInfo is null (still 200) at 1000+ appliances by default, and an unknown overlayId gives an all-zero matrix.
notes.GET /gms/topologyConfig/linkInfo/v2: Swagger describes linkInfo[status] as [[srcIndex, destIndex]] pairs; HPE reports links keyed by 'srcIdx,destIdx' strings, so check the actual shape. Answers 304 (no body) when the ETag is unchanged, which means unchanged, not empty.
notes.GET /gms/treeConfig: Scoped to the caller; under API-key auth the user is the key's name, so expect 200 {} (not 404), which does not prove no preferences exist. Body is a one-entry map keyed by username; unwrap it. Values are string digits: sort 1=IP 2=hostname, showAppliances 1=flat 2=nested, defaultOrganize 1=regions 2=groups.
notes.GET /gms/vti/cidr: Returns {ipAddress, mask}, the pool definition only. If no pool was ever saved, /gms/vti/cidr answers 503 "Failed to get VTI IP Pool Settings...", which is the normal fresh state, not an outage. With the subnets variant, reserved omitted = all, "true" = reserved only, "false" = unreserved only (case-sensitive; anything else returns {} at 200). reservedSubnets is a list with data, a dict when empty.
notes.GET /gms/wizard: Returns the stored blob verbatim, so it may carry keys beyond autoOpen. A 404 "Not found." means the wizard row does not exist (freshly initialized Orchestrator), not a fault.
notes.GET /gmsHostname: The body is {"gms_hostname": ...}. In container deployments it is the registration default that appliances dial (an IP or FQDN, not the OS hostname). The values 'Unknown', empty string and 'localhost' are unflagged placeholders meaning unavailable, not a real name.
notes.GET /gmsLicense: Read `code` in the body, not the HTTP status: an unlicensed Orchestrator returns 200 with code -1 ('Bad license key and no portal based license'); code 0 means licensed (key, portal, ECSP or metered). daysToExpiration is -999999 for never expires and -1 for expired; dates are epoch ms and expirationDate is 0 when unset. ECSP/metered report maxAppliances 1000000 with null expiry. Counts may be stale just after a restart.
notes.GET /gmsLicense/aas/token/stats: Returns empty rather than an error on non-AAS (non-subscription) deployments. Related reads: GET /gmsLicense/aas/token/usage and GET /gmsLicense/aas/token/display.
notes.GET /gmsOperatingSystem: Returns a plain-text string (not JSON): linux, windows or mac. Linux is the catch-all for anything not recognised as Windows or macOS, and unknown is unreachable. It describes only the host the Orchestrator JVM runs on, not a managed appliance, and cannot fail.
notes.GET /gmsOperatingSystem/root/passwordCha: A stored claim, not a check: the value is whatever was last POSTed. A missing row returns 200 {} (not 404, not false), ambiguous between never changed and never recorded. When set the body is {"passwordChanged": bool}.
notes.GET /gmsRemoteAuth: A single provider is read at GET /gmsRemoteAuth/<provider>, where the path segment is case-sensitive: RADIUS, TACACS+ (literal plus), SAML, OAuth or JWT; any other spelling is 404.
notes.GET /gmsRemoteAuth/type: Grouped summary {ThirdParty:{id:{name,loginType}} for RADIUS/TACACS+, OAuth:{...}, SAML:{...}}: which methods are configured and their display names, not full provider config. It is the picker the login page uses.
notes.GET /gmsSMTP: The password is nulled on read, and an unconfigured SMTP returns an empty object. The /gmsSMTP/validateServer call is a live connectivity probe returning {"isValidSMTPServer":bool}.
notes.GET /gmsSMTP/unverifiedEmails: Returns {unverifiedEmails: [...]}, flat address strings. [] does not mean everyone is verified: rows are only created while SMTP setting requireEmailVerification is on. A listed address may never have been mailed (the row is inserted before the SMTP check), and its outbound mail is withheld until verified. Password-reset and verification mails are auto-verified and never listed.
notes.GET /gmsserver/briefInfo: time is the server's clock as "d-MMM-yy HH:mm:ss z" in its own timezone, not ISO or UTC. uptime is a string like "2d 4h 13m 7s" ("0s" if non-positive). inGlpMode is false outside a container whatever the GLP setting; inContainerMode is the container check alone. The ETag includes time, so it changes about every second and a 304 is rare.
notes.GET /gmsserver/info: Null fields are omitted, so absent keys are normal. In container mode the host block (time, domain, host, osRev, memSize, numCpus, hwRev, disk, loadAverage) is skipped; on non-Linux hosts disk and load fields are the string 'Unknown'. model and platform fall back to 'UNKNOWN'. serverStartTime is epoch ms and disk figures are strings with a 'KB' suffix.
notes.GET /gmsserver/ping: dbHealth comes from a live database check, so a good reply confirms the database as well as the Orchestrator process.
notes.GET /haGroups: Returns an object keyed by group id, not a list. {} with 200 means no groups and cannot be told from HA never configured. This is the classic HA resource; EdgeHA is separate (GET /edge-ha/groups), so check both before concluding an appliance is not in HA.
notes.GET /health/alarmPeriodSummary: from/to are epoch milliseconds. Swagger marks applianceId required; HPE reports that omitting it returns the whole-fleet summary.
notes.GET /health/jitterPeriodSummary: Swagger says time is epoch seconds; HPE reports epoch milliseconds, so check against a known result. An empty object means no summary for that window. overlayId 0 is the underlay and -1 all overlays.
notes.GET /health/latencyPeriodSummary: Swagger says time is epoch seconds; HPE reports epoch milliseconds, so check against a known result. An empty object means no summary for that window. overlayId 0 is the underlay and -1 all overlays.
notes.GET /health/lossPeriodSummary: Swagger says time is epoch seconds; HPE reports epoch milliseconds, so check against a known result. An empty object means no summary for that window. overlayId 0 is the underlay and -1 all overlays.
notes.GET /health/mosPeriodSummary: Swagger says time is epoch seconds; HPE reports epoch milliseconds, so check against a known result. An empty object means no summary for that window. overlayId 0 is the underlay and -1 all overlays.
notes.GET /httpsCertificate: Per-appliance management certificate, distinct from the Orchestrator's own /gms/httpsCertificate. cached=true (default) reads the Orchestrator cache; false pulls live. Blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /ids/reservedsignature: Reserved signatures are the built-in, non-editable set the engine always applies. signature_family examples: 4.x, 5.x, 7.x.
notes.GET /ids/signatures: Catalog metadata only, without signature file payloads. signature_family values look like 4.x, 5.x, 7.x.
notes.GET /ids/signatures/profiles: config maps action to signature-rule ids and lists only rules that differ from the signature default, so an empty config means all defaults. signature_family shows 4.x when unset, but a filter drops profiles whose stored family is null; the filter is case-insensitive and an unmatched value gives an empty 200. A 400 'Request is invalid - supply correct input' most likely means a never-initialised Orchestrator.
notes.GET /ids/signatures/rules: signature_family can be 4.x, 5.x or 7.x (supported list at /ids/getSupportedSignatures); profile defaults to Default. filter matches free text against message and id. classtype and severity (low, medium, high) are matched case-insensitively; omit severity or send all for every level.
notes.GET /ids/state: Global, whole-fabric state: the result maps each IDS/IPS mode to a list of nePks, and there is no per-appliance filter (a nePk parameter would be ignored). Related GET /ids/config and GET /ids/autoSignatureUpdateState ({"auto":"on|off"}) are also global.
notes.GET /ikeless/config: On an unconfigured Orchestrator the first GET persists a default (seedLifeTimeDuration 0, maxActivationWaitTime null), so compare to None, not falsiness. Times are seconds. The body has no enabled flag, so it cannot show whether rotation is on, and scheduleConfig is not valid POST input (needs an {enabled, schedule} wrapper). 400 "Request is invalid" or 500s are stored-data faults.
notes.GET /ikeless/seedHistory: Despite the name this is one flat object of nine keys (new*, active*, currentActivationTime, previousActiveSeedId, previousActivationTime), not a list. Nulls are meaningful: new* null means no next seed yet, previous* null means fewer than two activations. Lifetimes are seconds (2147483647 = never expires); activation times are epoch ms. A new deployment returns 200 with all null.
notes.GET /interfaceState: Response is an ifInfo array; an ifname with a colon is a sub-interface (lan0:100), one starting bvi is a bridge virtual interface. cached must be exactly lowercase true/false; any other spelling (TRUE, 1) silently takes the live path. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" means never cached, retry cached=false. A successful live fetch overwrites the cache; any live failure is one 500.
notes.GET /ipObjects/addressGroup: With name it returns a single object; with a blank or absent name it returns an array of every group of that kind, with no marker of which. An unknown name gives 404 with an empty body, and an unparseable stored row is silently dropped and also gives that 404, so 404 means no readable group. Only the first row is visible if two share a name.
notes.GET /ipObjects/memoryConsumed: type must be addressgroups, servicegroups or all (trimmed, case-insensitive); any other value, including address or service, returns 200 with 0, so 0 can mean no groups or a misspelling. Empty type is 400 'Invalid query parameters'. The number is the byte size of distinct comma-joined group-name combinations in the flattened maps, not real memory, and all is not addressgroups plus servicegroups.
notes.GET /ipObjects/serviceGroup: With name it returns a single object; with a blank or absent name it returns an array of every group of that kind, with no marker of which. An unknown name gives 404 with an empty body, and an unparseable stored row is silently dropped and also gives that 404, so 404 means no readable group. Only the first row is visible if two share a name.
notes.GET /license/managementSettings: Six booleans (ec, cpx, nx, vx, vrx, saas) only tell the setup wizard which panels to show; they do not control licensing. Values are seeded once and never updated: all true usually means an upgraded Orchestrator, all false a fresh install, not what anyone chose. A missing row is a 404 with the plain text 'Not found.' (not JSON).
notes.GET /license/nx: Other license kinds are separate reads: /license/vx for VX-licensed appliances and /license/portal/appliance2 for Cloud Portal-granted ones, which also accepts a cached param (false = live from the portal).
notes.GET /license/portal/appliance/account: For a discovered (not yet managed) appliance use GET /license/portal/appliance/account/discovered?discoveredId instead of nePk. Provide exactly one of the two.
notes.GET /linkAggregation: cached=false on an appliance older than 9.0.3.0 gives 500 "Unsupported Version" (not valid JSON; a capability answer, not an outage); cached=true skips that check. A cached 404 with {"ERROR":"NOT_AVAILABLE"} is a remembered earlier live 404; the "may be unreachable" 404 is a plain cache miss, so retry cached=false. Only lowercase true uses the cache. Blank nePk 400, unknown nePk 500.
notes.GET /linkIntegrityTest/status: Status is per appliance, so a two-ended test needs a call for each nePk. Body is {active, result}; result is raw iperf/tcpperf console text whose layout differs by iperf2/iperf3, so read it rather than pattern-match. A 500 naming a hostname means the appliance did not answer; the generic 500 is usually an unknown nePk. Blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /liveTailLogger/getLoggers: feature is a closed list: CloudPortal, RouteLabel, AirGap. An unrecognised feature is not an error, it returns {"loggers":[]} with 200. Without feature the list contains only loggers registered so far in the running process, so it grows over time and two calls can differ; root and 10 special-config loggers are excluded.
notes.GET /logging: Returns {config:{members:...}, remote:{elements:[...]}}: the local logging config plus remote syslog receivers (elements empty when none). cached defaults true (last Orchestrator snapshot); false pulls live. Blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /loginSessions: Returns the raw session list; each SessionStatus has username, roles, auth source and session attributes. /session/activeSessions is the summarized user/IP/session-id view instead.
notes.GET /loopbackOrch: Not a single object: top-level keys are segment ids as strings ("0"), each with loopbackPool, interfaces and regionSettings (null when no per-region overrides). An empty map with 200 is what an unconfigured Orchestrator returns. A 400 'Request is invalid' despite no input means the stored setting row cannot be parsed, a server-side data fault.
notes.GET /loopbackOrch/pool: Besides per-segment/region/subnet pool allocation, it includes a nested map of historical (reclaimable) record counts keyed segment, then region, then subnet.
notes.GET /loopbackOrch/pool/history: Records are freed addresses still awaiting reclaim. Only seg is used here; the sibling paths /loopbackOrch/pool/historySegReg?seg&reg and /historySegRegPool?seg&reg&pool narrow by region and by subnet (subnet CIDR sent as `pool`).
notes.GET /mgmtServices: Management services exposed by the appliance (SSH, HTTPS, SNMP), not the /gms/services policy list. cached=true with no stored row gives 404 'may be unreachable', but the appliance is never contacted, so it just means never polled; retry cached=false, which writes the cache. An nePk unknown to Orchestrator gives a bare 500 'There was an internal server error.', not 404.
notes.GET /nac: Despite being a GET, cached=false polls the appliance and overwrites the stored row. Response is {nePk, nac}. Cached 404 "may be unreachable" only means no cached NAC config, or an unknown nePk (indistinguishable). 204 means the stored row is empty. A live failure 500 names the hostname, not the nePk.
notes.GET /nat/maps: Both halves return the appliance JSON verbatim. cached is matched as the exact string 'true'; any other spelling (TRUE, 1) silently goes live, and live fetches refresh the cache. On the cached path a 404 'Appliance with key ... may be unreachable' is usually just a cache miss: retry cached=false. Maps and pools are cached separately, so one can 404 while the other has data. Error bodies are text/html.
notes.GET /nat/natPools: Both halves return the appliance JSON verbatim. cached is matched as the exact string 'true'; any other spelling (TRUE, 1) silently goes live, and live fetches refresh the cache. On the cached path a 404 'Appliance with key ... may be unreachable' is usually just a cache miss: retry cached=false. Maps and pools are cached separately, so one can 404 while the other has data. Error bodies are text/html.
notes.GET /natAll: cached is tested as exact 'true' (default true only when absent); any other spelling goes live, and a live fetch writes the cache. The cache-miss 404 'may be unreachable' is just an empty cache; retry with cached=false. natMaps keeps all fields but, for appliances older than 8.1.0.0, rewrites only match index 0 to the new format; natAll is a raw passthrough, and the two can fail independently.
notes.GET /natMaps: cached is tested as exact 'true' (default true only when absent); any other spelling goes live, and a live fetch writes the cache. The cache-miss 404 'may be unreachable' is just an empty cache; retry with cached=false. natMaps keeps all fields but, for appliances older than 8.1.0.0, rewrites only match index 0 to the new format; natAll is a raw passthrough, and the two can fail independently.
notes.GET /natMapsDynamic: A 500 'Failed to load appliance data' covers an unknown nePk, a conversion fault and other errors alike, so check the nePk first (a blank nePk is a clean 400). A cached 404 'not found. It may be unreachable' only means nothing is stored; retry cached=false, which also refills the cache.
notes.GET /neighbors: Cached 404 "may be unreachable" on a never-polled appliance means the cache is empty (no live fallback); cached=false fetches live and refreshes the cache. Live: an appliance 404 stays 404, other failures are 500 with the same message. Body is re-serialized JSON; invalid JSON is 500 "Invalid JSON response from appliance.". An empty stored row gives neighbors None. Blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /netFlow: Raw passthrough of the stored or appliance JSON, unvalidated. Cached 404 "may be unreachable" is just a cache miss (no automatic live fallback); cached=false fetches live and refreshes the cache for later cached reads. Any live failure collapses to one 500 "<hostname>: Failed to get data from appliance.". Only the exact string true means cached; other spellings go live.
notes.GET /notification: configData is {notificationMessage, loginMessage}: notificationMessage is the in-app banner for logged-in users, loginMessage the text on the login page. Empty or absent means no banner is configured.
notes.GET /optimizationMaps: Orchestrator re-parses the policy, so it is lossy: only match/set index 0 survives and unknown keys are dropped. netmem_mode is an int (0 disabled, 1 balanced, 2 minimize latency, 3 maximize reduction); proxy_type is none, tcp-only, ssl, srdf or iscsi. A 200 whose whole body is a bare number (e.g. 404) means the appliance rejected a live call. cached=false repopulates the cache; the cache-miss 404 'may be unreachable' is just an empty cache.
notes.GET /orch-ha/info: info.mode is NORMAL (stand-alone), HA_PRIMARY (active) or HA_BACKUP (standby: health-check only, limited REST API). In NORMAL mode currentInstance and primaryInstance are present but JSON null. An instance named but not yet registered comes back as a placeholder with name and ipAddress 'unknown' and registerTime/lastCheckin 0. /orch-ha/instances without an id returns a list of all registered instances.
notes.GET /orch-ha/instances: info.mode is NORMAL (stand-alone), HA_PRIMARY (active) or HA_BACKUP (standby: health-check only, limited REST API). In NORMAL mode currentInstance and primaryInstance are present but JSON null. An instance named but not yet registered comes back as a placeholder with name and ipAddress 'unknown' and registerTime/lastCheckin 0. /orch-ha/instances without an id returns a list of all registered instances.
notes.GET /orch-ha/notificationConfig: Returns {enabledEmailNotification, emailAddress, checkinFailureThreshold}. This GET writes: if no config row exists it creates one with defaults (false, emailAddress null, threshold 2) and returns them. A null emailAddress cannot be posted straight back, since the write validates the address.
notes.GET /orch-ha/primary/status: Returns {primaryStatus}. 400 "Orchestrator is not in HA mode" on a non-HA node. Asked on the primary itself the answer is hardcoded true with no probe. Only a backup really probes (HTTPS GET of the primary's /gmsserver/ping on 443), and any failure just reads false, so down and unreachable-from-here are indistinguishable.
notes.GET /orch-ha/reachability: Unconfigured is not an error: customDefaultReachability and reachabilityForLabel both come back null, never a 404 or empty object. customDefaultReachability maps each HA instance id to the IP or DNS name others use; reachabilityForLabel overrides it per interface label with labelId and priority. Works in NORMAL mode too but has nothing meaningful to report.
notes.GET /ospf/config/allVrfs/interfaces: Result is keyed per VRF segment, unlike the default-VRF OSPF reads. Intended for appliances running OSPF inside multiple segments.
notes.GET /ospf/config/allVrfs/system: Result is keyed per VRF segment, unlike the default-VRF OSPF reads. Intended for appliances running OSPF inside multiple segments.
notes.GET /ospf/state/system: The full OSPF operational view is split across /ospf/state/system, /ospf/state/interfaces (per-interface adjacency) and /ospf/state/neighbors, all taking nePk and fromGms. Default is live (fromGms false); fromGms=true reads the Orchestrator cache. A blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /overlayManagerProperties: ipsecPresharedKey is always null, which says nothing about whether a key exists. A 200 with {} means never written, not defaults. settings is keyed by WAN interface-label id and only used when overwriteExistingTunnels is true. enableInterRegionRouting null means never explicitly set; enableTemplateApply may be inherited from enable. ikelessSeed is deprecated.
notes.GET /pauseOrchestration: Bare array of nePk strings; an empty array is the normal never-configured state. Paused appliances still sync and report state but skip overlay/tunnel, SASE, advanced security, shell access, HA supernet, end-entity profile, secure web services and cipher profile config. The list also acts as a blacklist for Netskope, Zscaler, Azure VWAN and AWS TGNM polling. A 500 means corrupt stored config.
notes.GET /portForwarding: HPE reports cached is read as the exact string 'true' and defaults to true only when absent (Swagger says omitted means live); any other value goes live and refreshes the cache. Result is re-parsed: ports are strings, unknown fields dropped, vrf_id and srcIf backfilled (0, ""), so an explicit Default-segment rule looks unset. A cached 404 'may be unreachable' is usually a cache miss; a corrupt cached row gives 400.
notes.GET /portProfiles/config: The result is the Orchestrator's re-parsed model, not the stored bytes: unknown keys are dropped and defaults backfilled, so a field's presence or absence proves nothing. `label` is an interface-label ID string; `harden` is a string enum (0 Allow All, 1 IPSEC Only, 2 Stateful, 3 Stateful+SNAT); zone 0 can mean never set or deleted. Order is unspecified; one corrupt row makes the whole list a 500. Do not post this config to an appliance.
notes.GET /portProfiles/isLabelInUse: Returns {"labelId","side","inUse":{"inUse":bool,"portProfileIds":[...]}}, with the boolean nested under inUse.inUse. Only router-mode profiles are scanned, so bridge-mode profiles are missed and false does not prove the label is unused. side is wan or lan, case-insensitive, and an unrecognised value just returns false.
notes.GET /qosMaps: Response is Orchestrator's re-parsed model, not raw appliance JSON: only index 0 of match/set is kept, unknown keys are dropped, and options defaults plus gms_marked:false are injected. An unknown structured match criterion makes it a 500. Cached 404 is a cache miss, not unreachable; cached=false refreshes the cache. A 503 comes back with no detail.
notes.GET /rbac/allowedRestApis: method is reduced to letters, upper-cased and must be a known HTTP method (400 otherwise). An API key that is not in the RBAC key map gives 404; a caller with no roles or asset gets {}.
notes.GET /rbac/assignment: Without username the result is an array; with one it is a single object. roles is a comma-joined string; listOfRoles is a derived trimmed list. An unknown username returns 204 with no body, not 404. An empty username returns every mapping; a whitespace-only username is 400. No ordering or paging.
notes.GET /rbac/legacyApi: Rows are rewrite rules, not an allow-list: a request is retried only after it returned 404/405 with JSON or no content type. params and body are JSON-encoded strings needing a second parse. Order is undefined, first match wins. This GET returns the whole table even when advanced property enableLegacyApisSupport is off; turning it on needs a restart to take effect.
notes.GET /rbac/role: These are menu-permission roles (which UI menus a role can access), not the appliance-access role names returned by GET /roles.
notes.GET /reachability/appliance: 404 'may be unreachable' on /reachability/gms means Orchestrator has no row for that nePk (mistyped or deleted), not that the appliance is down; an unreachable one still returns 200 with state 2. state is an integer: 0 unknown, 1 normal, 2 unreachable, 3 unsupported version, 4 out of sync, 5 sync in progress. /reachability/appliance gives a bare 500 for an unknown nePk; a hostname in the 500 means the nePk was valid and the device failed.
notes.GET /reachability/gms: 404 'may be unreachable' on /reachability/gms means Orchestrator has no row for that nePk (mistyped or deleted), not that the appliance is down; an unreachable one still returns 200 with state 2. state is an integer: 0 unknown, 1 normal, 2 unreachable, 3 unsupported version, 4 out of sync, 5 sync in progress. /reachability/appliance gives a bare 500 for an unknown nePk; a hostname in the 500 means the nePk was valid and the device failed.
notes.GET /reachability/gms2: Not passive: it sends a live request to the appliance over the portal WebSocket. A 400 'Invalid nePk' means Orchestrator's cache does not hold that appliance, not that it is down. `state` is an integer (0 UNKNOWN, 1 NORMAL, 2 UNREACHABLE, 3 UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, 4 OUT_OF_SYNC, 5 SYNC_IN_PROGRESS). lastMessageReceived is absent when gmsWs is Not Connected; pingFrequency and wsMaxIdleTime can be a number, 'Unknown' or '-'.
notes.GET /reachability/gms2/appliancesReachab: Probes every appliance live, serially, so it is slow on large fabrics. One appliance cached without a database row makes the whole call 500, which does not mean the fabric is unhealthy. state is a name (NORMAL, UNREACHABLE, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, OUT_OF_SYNC, SYNC_IN_PROGRESS, UNKNOWN). Each entry has only hostName, state, gmsWs and portalWs. A missing appliance is one Orchestrator is not holding, not one that is down.
notes.GET /regions: Regions group appliances for regional mesh/hub topology in overlays. GET /regions/appliances takes nePk and returns that appliance's region association.
notes.GET /regions/appliances: Regions group appliances for regional mesh/hub topology in overlays. GET /regions/appliances takes nePk and returns that appliance's region association.
notes.GET /release: Lists only builds the portal has published: {"releases": {"gmsbuilds": [...], "vxoabuilds": [...]}}, each build with a `version`.
notes.GET /release/notifications: While the background release-info job is still running this returns an empty list, not an error, so retry after it finishes.
notes.GET /remoteLogReceiver: Unknown receiverId or no receivers gives 204, not 404 or []. receiverType: 0 HTTP, 1 HTTPS, 2 KAFKA, 3 SYSLOG, 4 WEBSOCKET; logType: 0 AUDIT_LOG, 1 ALARM, 2 ACTIVE_ALARM_RESUBMISSION. With receiverId, headerValue comes back in clear text (blanked in the list); a WEBSOCKET key is always clear. A WEBSOCKET url containing '<orchestratorIpOrDomainName>' means no usable Orchestrator address.
notes.GET /remoteLogReceiver/sequenceId/latest: logType accepts only alarm or auditLog; any other value is a 404, not a 400 (blank is 400). Matching is asymmetric: alarm is case-sensitive ('Alarm' gives 404) while auditLog is case-insensitive ('auditlog' works).
notes.GET /remoteLogReceiver/websocket/status: Returns 204 or empty when there is nothing to report. The companion GET /remoteLogReceiver/syncQueueStatus shows the outbound sync-queue backlog.
notes.GET /reports: Without id it returns the JSON metadata list. With id it returns the report file as a binary octet-stream attachment, not JSON, so do not read it as text.
notes.GET /resolver: cached is tested as exact 'true' (default true only when absent); other spellings go live, and a live fetch writes the cache. The cache-miss 404 'may be unreachable' is just an empty cache; retry cached=false. /resolver and /dnsProxy/config are cached independently, so one can 404 while the other returns data. /resolver live failures are always 500, even for an unknown nePk. Error bodies are text/html.
notes.GET /restApiConfig: Returns a {flagName: bool} map. The main flag is communicateWithApplianceViaPortal (Orchestrator reaches appliances via the Cloud Portal); a newly created default row sets it true.
notes.GET /restRequestTimeStats: Swagger marks resource and method required; HPE reports them as optional filters, with nePk the only mandatory one (400 otherwise). from/to are epoch milliseconds and to=0 means now. portalWS selects the channel: true is the portal websocket, false the direct websocket.
notes.GET /restRequestTimeStats/summary: nePk defaults to 'all' when omitted. portalWS=true selects the portal WebSocket channel, false the direct WebSocket. from and to are epoch milliseconds; to=0 means now.
notes.GET /roles: These are user-defined RBAC appliance-access roles that gate which appliances a user or API key may reach, not the built-in user role display names. An invalid pattern is 400 "Invalid role name pattern".
notes.GET /roles/nextId: The endpoint answers {"nextId": N}. It is a suggestion, not a reservation: only saving roles advances it, so concurrent readers get the same id. It can return an id already taken: 1 on a fresh Orchestrator (0 default and 1 unknown are built in), and 2 after the scan wraps at 255 or when 2-255 are all used. Check the id against the existing roles.
notes.GET /routeLabels/nextId: Both endpoints answer {"nextId": N}. nextId is a suggestion, not a reservation: it can return an id already in use (2 on a never-saved Orchestrator, or 2 after the scan wraps at 127; ids 0 and 1 are never offered), so check against the existing labels. versionCounter is the minimum `version` for any new label id; a lower one is rejected with 400 'Label version must be greater than or equal to the current version'.
notes.GET /routeLabels/versionCounter: Both endpoints answer {"nextId": N}. nextId is a suggestion, not a reservation: it can return an id already in use (2 on a never-saved Orchestrator, or 2 after the scan wraps at 127; ids 0 and 1 are never offered), so check against the existing labels. versionCounter is the minimum `version` for any new label id; a lower one is rejected with 400 'Label version must be greater than or equal to the current version'.
notes.GET /routeMaps: Response is Orchestrator's re-parsed model {options, data}: containers defaulted, unknown fields dropped, and for appliances older than 8.1.0.0 rules are rewritten to the new string-matching format, so it is not the literal appliance config. Any conversion failure, including an unknown nePk, is a 500 "Failed to load appliance data"; only a blank nePk is 400. Cached 404 is a cache miss; cached=false refreshes the cache.
notes.GET /saMap: Live passthrough to the appliance, so it fails if the appliance is unreachable. An unknown nePk is a generic 500 'There was an internal server error.', not a 404. A bare 404 with empty body relayed from the appliance is the normal answer for an appliance with no SA map; other appliance failures are 500 prefixed with the hostname.
notes.GET /secureWebServicesConfig: Response is synthesized: {secureWebServicesConfig, isWebccSupported}. /scalars is read first, so its failure blocks the config. isWebccSupported false only means not proven supported. Null fields are real (appliance omitted them). Cached 404 "may be unreachable" is just a cache miss; cached=false fetches live and refreshes the cache for later cached reads.
notes.GET /security/cipherProfile: Response holds a profiles list and a supportedCipherSuites map, fetched independently, so one may hold {error} while the other has data. Both empty means not configured, never null or 404. A profile with editable=false cannot be updated (the PUT gives 500). Suite fields are snake_case (key_exchange, hmac, encryption_algo, ossl_name), profile fields camelCase. Failures are plain-text 500; reachable only with the Cipher Settings menu grant.
notes.GET /security/cipherProfile/activeProfil: No active profile (empty list, none active, or never written) is 200 with an empty body, not 404. At most one profile is active. Any failure is 500 with a plain-text body. This url is granted under several menus, so it can succeed for a session that gets 403 from the base cipher-profile read.
notes.GET /security/cipherProfile/defaultCiphe: Despite the name this is a catalogue of allowed values, not a default profile: about 25 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE lists such as TLS_CIPHER_SUITES, IKE_HASH_ALGORITHMS, IKE_DH_GROUPS. With no config row it returns 200 with an empty body, not 404; real failures are plain-text 500. It is readable under several menus, so it can succeed where /security/cipherProfile returns a bare 403.
notes.GET /security/ddos/protectionProfiles/ap: With cached=false, an appliance whose software lacks DDoS protection profiles returns HTTP 200 with the body {"ERROR": "NOT_AVAILABLE"}, not a 404; check for that sentinel.
notes.GET /security/endEntityProfiles: Profiles are templates for certificate requests; there is no validity or lifetime field (the CA decides). Key fields: label, purpose (sd_wan, tls_server, tls_client, general), csr_attrs (e.g. rsa_2048_with_sha256), est_server_profiles (priority 0-3 to name). Unset fields are omitted, not null; gms_marked is always true here and est is derived from the EST map. Order is unsorted.
notes.GET /security/estServer: password and challenge_password are never returned, so set and unset look identical. Keys are snake_case and vary per row (nulls omitted); port defaults 443 and retry_interval 300 seconds when unsaved. Max 32 configs. Failure is a plain-text 500 "Failed to fetch EST config", not JSON.
notes.GET /securityMaps: cached is compared to the string 'true'; any other spelling (TRUE, 1) silently takes the live path. A cached 404 'not found. It may be unreachable' usually means nothing is cached yet; retry cached=false, which also refills the cache. Returns raw stored JSON with priority keys as strings; a missing field may mean an older appliance version.
notes.GET /session/activeSessions: Rows are {type, idle_time, login_time, remote_host, username, roles, authSource} with no session id; (username, login_time) is the only identity. login_time is epoch seconds, idle_time is seconds. `roles` is the raw role names for RBAC users but 'Read-Write'/'Read-Only' for others (not the 'Admin Manager'/'Network Monitor' strings in /users). authSource is the login protocol, or the provider name for OAuth. MTO SSO sessions are omitted.
notes.GET /shaper: The inbound shaper is a separate read at GET /inboundShaper with the same nePk and cached params; /shaper is outbound.
notes.GET /snatMaps: cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" usually means this resource was never polled, not that the appliance is down; retry cached=false, which also refreshes the cache. Unknown nePk is an opaque 500.
notes.GET /snmp: Raw passthrough of the appliance JSON, unvalidated. cached must be exactly lowercase true/false; other spellings (TRUE, 1) silently take the live path. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" just means never cached; retry cached=false. A successful live read overwrites the cache. Any live failure is one 500 "<hostname>: Failed to get data from appliance."; blank nePk is 400.
notes.GET /spPortal/account/key/changeStatus: Returns generateTimestamp and committedToPortalTimestamp. It is 400 in Air-Gap mode (rotation must be done from the Air-Gap Application); for the primary account it also 400s if the Orchestrator is not registered with the portal, and an unknown secondaryAccountName is 404.
notes.GET /spPortal/appExpressAppConfig: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/applianceWSStatus: Live probe on every call: /hello over the portal WS and /helloDirectWS over the direct WS. Returns {nePk, wsStatus:{portalWS, directWS}}, each {reachable, err}. reachable false with err null (portalWS) means no portal WS adapter existed and no probe was attempted. A failed probe is still 200. Unknown nePk is 404 with plain text "Invalid nePk.".
notes.GET /spPortal/applicationTags: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/broadcastMessage: The body is an envelope (resourceBase, resourceKey, configData, version, timestamp in epoch ms); the notice text is at configData[0].message. No banner is normally 200 with configData [] (truthy, so test configData); 204 means no row yet or Orchestrator not registered with the portal. A damaged row comes back as 200 with non-JSON text.
notes.GET /spPortal/compoundClassification: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/config: Returns portal credentials in cleartext (registration.key, oldKey, and key/oldKey of each secondaryAccounts entry) even to a read-only role; treat the response as secret. Top-level accountId is synthesized and can differ from registration.accountId. port=0 or empty strings mean never configured. No stored row gives an opaque 500, not 404; a corrupt row gives 400.
notes.GET /spPortal/connectivity: Returns {portal: int}; 0 means not connected, but in Air-gap mode it is always 0 because no ping is attempted, so 0 is not necessarily a broken link.
notes.GET /spPortal/connectivity/appliance: portalUrl is just the host (400 if blank); the backend appends the configured portal port. /spPortal/connectivity/orchestrator returns {"portal": <int>} where 0 means not reachable. /spPortal/connectivity/appliance probes each appliance with a 30s timeout; HPE says no download is made, where Swagger describes a URL download test.
notes.GET /spPortal/connectivity/orchestrator: portalUrl is just the host (400 if blank); the backend appends the configured portal port. /spPortal/connectivity/orchestrator returns {"portal": <int>} where 0 means not reachable. /spPortal/connectivity/appliance probes each appliance with a 30s timeout; HPE says no download is made, where Swagger describes a URL download test.
notes.GET /spPortal/dnsClassification: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/internetDb/geoLocateIp: Pass ip as the decimal 32-bit integer (8.8.8.8 is 134744072), not a dotted quad: the value is pasted unquoted into a JSON body, so a dotted quad gives 400 "Request is invalid - supply correct input" or a portal-side failure. Proxied live to the Cloud Portal, so portal registration and connectivity are required. Do not send a blank ip.
notes.GET /spPortal/internetDb/ipIntelligence: limit <= 0 or > 10000 becomes 10000, not none; start below 0 becomes 0. An empty page [] may only mean the table is not populated: the GET starts the INTERNET_DB job (only when start < limit), so retry later.
notes.GET /spPortal/internetDb/ipIntelligence/: ip is a 32-bit unsigned integer (0 to 4294967295), not a dotted quad. If filter is given it takes precedence (case-insensitive substring) and ip is ignored. Sending neither param silently searches IP 0, so always send exactly one. Response is {"results":[...]}.
notes.GET /spPortal/internetDb/serviceIdToSaas: Filter precedence: serviceIds, then matchAny, then org, else top-N (top is ignored with serviceIds). serviceIds must be digits separated by single commas; an empty or non-numeric token (e.g. a trailing comma) gives 500. {} means the database is not populated yet: this GET starts the population job, so retry shortly.

saasApps is distinct SaaS app names; count is distinct service ids (normally larger), so do not report it as an app count. An empty database gives [] for saasApps and {"count":0} for count (still 200) and triggers a background portal refresh that does nothing on an unregistered Orchestrator. User-defined entries are merged into both.

Returns an object keyed by country name, each value an array of 8 strings [serviceId, saasId, country, countryCode, org, appName, displayName, priority]. Only one arbitrary row per country backs the other fields, so use it as a country picklist, not a summary. countryCode can be null. {} is not an error: it means an empty table, and may be permanent if the Orchestrator is not registered with the Cloud Portal.

saasApps is distinct SaaS app names; count is distinct service ids (normally larger), so do not report it as an app count. An empty database gives [] for saasApps and {"count":0} for count (still 200) and triggers a background portal refresh that does nothing on an unregistered Orchestrator. User-defined entries are merged into both.
notes.GET /spPortal/meterFlowClassification: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/portProtocolClassification: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/registration/account: Returns an object {pendingPoll, msg, secondaryAccounts:[{accountName, accountKey, emails, registered, msg}]}, not a list; accountKey is plaintext, treat as secret. The list follows registration-status entries, so a newly configured account is absent until a registration cycle runs, and empty can also mean the status read failed (still 200). After the POST, poll until pendingPoll is false. Top-level msg and emails are volatile and lost on restart.
notes.GET /spPortal/saasClassification: Each classification template has an /info sibling returning {"hashVal": "<string>"} for change polling ("0" if not computed). Empty is "[]" for dnsClassification and meterFlowClassification but "{}" for the others. Except appExpressAppConfig, an empty read triggers a populating job, so these GETs are not side-effect-free.
notes.GET /spPortal/trafficBehavior: {} means the data has not been computed yet; the call also starts the TRAFFIC_BEHAVIOR_JOB to populate it, so retry shortly.

notes.GET /subnets: /subnets/all returns the full learned/advertised subnet table and takes no cached param (always live); /subnets honours cached.
notes.GET /subnets/all: /subnets/all returns the full learned/advertised subnet table and takes no cached param (always live); /subnets honours cached.
notes.GET /subnets/forDiscovered: discoveredId must be the integer id of an existing discovered appliance, otherwise 400 "Invalid discovered appliance id". Returns the live route-all table, reached over the portal/UUID discovery channel.
notes.GET /systemInfo: cached=true returns an extrapolated uptime (an estimate) plus uptimeString; cached=false is the appliance's raw reply with no uptimeString and refreshes the cache. A cache miss, corrupt row or dead appliance all give the same misleading 500 mentioning a discovered appliance; retry cached=false. Missing nePk is a 500, not 400. Any cached value other than lowercase true goes live.
notes.GET /systemInfo/system: systemConfig is the stored /system config forwarded as-is: normally a parsed object, but a corrupt row still returns 200, so check it is an object. Unknown nePk is a 500 "Failed to get basic data from GMS, NE: <nePk>" meaning no cached /system row, not an outage. cached=false pulls live and overwrites the cached row. Not the same as the /systemInfo summary.
notes.GET /tca: cached=true reads only the Orchestrator cache: 404 "may be unreachable" just means nothing is cached yet (retry cached=false), and a 204 means a cached row with no data, not zero TCA rules. cached=false queries the appliance and also saves the answer to the cache. Unknown nePk and an appliance failure both give a 500; blank nePk is 400 "Invalid nePk".
notes.GET /tcpdump/status: Raw appliance status: expect active (bool), progress (0..1), lastOneDone (bool), status. progress null means accepted but not started yet. Unknown nePk is a generic 500, not 404; a failing appliance gives 500 prefixed with its hostname. Capture is single-flight fleet-wide: while any capture runs, starting another via /tcpdump/run fails with 500 even for a different appliance.
notes.GET /tcpdump/tcpdumpStatus: Returns the poll handle (a UUID) as text/html. An empty string is the normal idle answer, not an error. The key resets to empty as soon as the capture finishes, so save it while running. It is global for the whole Orchestrator, not per appliance.
notes.GET /template/applianceAssociation: applianceAssociation maps nePk to template-group names (field templateIds holds names, not ids); an appliance with no associations has no key. templateGroupsPriorities is a global list, index 0 applies first; a group not listed ranks by that appliance's group count, so it can outrank a deeply listed one. notes.GET /template/history: latestOnly is required on /template/history: omitted gives 500, any value other than exact true gives 200 with a null body. Only the latest apply per (nePk, templateGroup, templateName) is kept, and /template/history lists successful ones only while groupList is unfiltered, so a group with no rows means its applies failed. templateName "" rows are group markers. appliedOn is epoch ms.
notes.GET /template/history/groupList: latestOnly is required on /template/history: omitted gives 500, any value other than exact true gives 200 with a null body. notes.GET /template/templateGroups: namesOnly=true gives a list of names; otherwise full group objects with encrypted fields scrubbed, so never post the result back (it blanks credentials). With templateGroup set, namesOnly is ignored and you get a one-group list. An unknown group name is 500 'Failed to get Templates for group:<name>', not 404. A missing qosMaps template means not licensed. lastSaved is epoch ms.
