notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/arubaCentral/sit: sitesMapping is a list of single-key objects {siteId: [appliances]}, with null (not []) for a site without appliances. Entries are {nePk, applianceName, recommendSite, gmsMarked}; gmsMarked true means manually pinned, false means auto-assigned by proximity; site id 0 means unmapped. Corrupt stored data silently truncates the list with 200, so a missing site does not prove it has no appliances.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/arubaCentral/sub: password is blanked in the response. A 404 means no subscription is configured. A related connectivity check reports CONNECTED whenever a valid refresh or access token exists in the database, not from a live probe.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/awstgnm/interfac: A list of lists: [[primary label ids], [backup label ids]]. Group 1 is always empty in practice (backup is rejected for AWS). [] means never configured; two empty groups means configured to nothing, which raises the AWS_NO_INTERFACES_CONFIGURED alarm.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/awstgnm/pauseOrc: Returns {"pauseOrchestration":{"paused":bool}}. Unlike sibling pause reads this one answers from an in-memory cache refreshed by event, so a read right after a write, or on the other HA node, can show the old value. false is ambiguous: never configured, explicitly resumed, and a corrupt config row all read false.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/awstgnm/pollingI: Returns {"pollingInterval":seconds}. The UI shows minutes (UI 240 = 14400 here). If never saved it returns 14400 (4 hours) without storing it, so default and explicitly set look the same, and a value does not prove a polling job exists. Send seconds back on write.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/awstgnm/tunnelSe: Result is a map keyed by interface-label ID, not one object. Never-configured, configured-to-defaults and a corrupt stored row all return the same plausible default map with 200, so they cannot be told apart. A label added since the last save is missing from the stored map. presharedKey is returned in clear text.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/applianceAs: The only top-level key is enabled, a list of {nePk, priority, lastUpdateTime}; nePk is inside each entry, not a map key. Empty list means no appliance associated. This GET writes: if the config row is missing it creates and persists {enabled: []} instead of returning 404.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/defaultTunn: Both paths return one object shared by every HPE SSE label. defaultTunnelSetting is a hard-coded baseline, not what is in force. tunnelSettings saves the factory defaults if none are stored, so this GET can write. A read failure comes back as 200 with an empty body. Null fields are omitted; a short key set usually means a partial full-replace save.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/interfaces: The groups are positional lists of interface label IDs (not names): index 0 primary, 1 backup, 2 secondary. Three empty lists are returned when nothing is stored, but a stored value comes back as saved, so fewer groups are possible; check length before indexing. A read failure also looks like three empty lists, so empty is not proof of no config. A label in no group is skipped.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/ipslaSettin: Unconfigured Orchestrators report enableIpslaRuleOrchestration true, so true cannot tell explicitly enabled from never set. An unparseable stored setting is a 500 'Failed to parse ipsla setting'. GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/ipslaRuleDestination likewise returns a hard-coded default (http-monitor to https://sp-ipsla.silverpeak.cloud) when nothing is stored, so a 200 does not mean it was configured.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/pauseOrches: Returns {"paused": bool}. false is ambiguous: never configured, explicitly resumed, or a corrupt config row (parse errors are swallowed). This route reads the config table and is authoritative; cache-based views such as /cache/syncState can disagree until the cache refreshes. Pausing only writes the flag and does not queue appliances for re-orchestration. A role without the Axis menu gets a bare 403.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/pollingInte: Value is pollingInterval in seconds (the UI shows minutes; 600 = 10 minutes). This GET is not side-effect free: when no interval is stored it persists the default 600 and creates or updates the HPE SSE polling job, and a failed save is only logged, so the 600 may not be saved.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/popOverride: Map of nePk to labelId to {pop1, pop2} (IPv4 or FQDN; a half-written entry omits the missing key). {} at 200 means nothing is overridden. Appliances whose overrides were all deleted are excluded, so this cannot enumerate the fleet. One malformed stored row makes the whole call 500. labelId must be a WAN interface label.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/subLocation: invalidRule is computed per request; true usually means a referenced appliance, group, region, zone, label or address group was deleted, and dead references are still listed. id is the 1-based position and shifts whenever the list is saved, so do not cache it. Read errors are swallowed and return a partial list with 200, so a short or empty array does not prove no rules. Order is unspecified.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/subscriptio: apiTokenKey is nulled on read, so null does not show whether one is set. 404 means no subscription exists.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/axis/tunnelSetti: Both paths return one object shared by every HPE SSE label. defaultTunnelSetting is a hard-coded baseline, not what is in force. tunnelSettings saves the factory defaults if none are stored, so this GET can write. A read failure comes back as 200 with an empty body. Null fields are omitted; a short key set usually means a partial full-replace save.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/connectivi: connectivity is an int: 0 NOT_CONNECTED, 1 CONNECTED. Only 0 or 1 is ever returned, and every failure (bad credentials, Azure unreachable) is 0 at HTTP 200, so 0 does not say why. This GET has side effects: it probes Azure live and raises or clears the FAILED_TO_CONNECT_TO_AZURE alarm.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/interfaces: Returns a list of lists of WAN interface-label ids: [0] primary, [1] backup. Only group 0 is used (first label matching a deployment wins, later ids are fallback). Unconfigured returns [] (not 404). A saved body with no `ids` key poisons the row so every later GET returns a bare 500; saving a valid value again clears it. Separate from the LAN-side setting.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/lan-side-c: Returns a list with one entry per appliance and snake_case fields nepk, priority, vhub_id, routeserver_id, loadbalancer_id, timestamp; the three *_id fields are lists. priority is stored but unused. A row whose id columns fail to parse comes back with empty lists and timestamp 0, indistinguishable from unassociated. This GET is the only reliable confirmation of a write, since the POST can return 200 even when the DB write failed.

One global rule list, no per-appliance read. Response azureConfiguration null at 200 means the read failed; [] means no rules. Unset fields are absent, not null. Array order is unspecified, yet the first matching rule wins (nePk, then region, then group, then all), so an early `all` rule can shadow others. The matching POST is a full replace: rules whose id is omitted are deleted.

Lists what Orchestrator has provisioned (resourceType vHub, routeServer or loadBalancer, case-sensitive), not Azure discovery. No filters; one row per interface label, so nepk+azureArtifactId repeats. [] is normal. Load-balancer rows vanish if the appliance hostname changed. A short array can mean silently dropped rows. Rows persist for deleted appliances until cleanup.

Live read of appliance BGP state, segment 0 only. [] or 204 means no vHub/route-server association (load-balancer-only appliances too) or a failed poll. connectionStatus: Up, "1 of 2 Up", Down, Unknown, Pending (appliance unreachable/unknown/unsupported, skipped). Down with empty bgpStatus means not evaluated. Route-server azure_name is always {}.

Live probe, not cached: it logs into Azure and raises or clears the FAILED_TO_CONNECT_TO_AZURE_LAN alarm, even while LAN-side orchestration is paused. Values are integers: 0 not connected, 1 connected, 3 insufficient permissions (2 is never emitted). vwanHub and routeServer come from one call and always match. No subscription configured also shows as 0. Always 200.

Returns the stored account (id, name, subscriptionId, tenantId, clientId, clientSecret, comment); clientSecret is always null. A bare 404 with no body means LAN-side automation is not configured. A malformed stored blob is 400 "Request is invalid - supply correct input", not 500.

Reads Orchestrator's cached list and never contacts Azure; a background job refreshes it (default every 4 hours) and it freezes silently while LAN-side is paused. [] means none discovered, never polled, or cache wiped, not proof none exist. A pool with several backend addresses shows only the last ipAddress/virtualNetwork, which are absent when null.

Body carries paused (bool). false is ambiguous: never configured looks the same as explicitly resumed. A corrupt or key-less stored row is a 500. This is a separate flag from the Azure VWAN pause, though both share one RBAC menu. Pausing or resuming queues the whole appliance fleet for re-orchestration.

Value is lanSidePollingInterval in seconds (default 14400 = 4 hours; the UI shows minutes). It can be JSON null when a stored row lacks the key, which means malformed config, not polling off. There is no write endpoint for this value. A malformed stored blob gives 400 'Request is invalid - supply correct input', not 500.

regions is a flat map of regionId to display name like '(US) East US'. A 200 with JSON null means the Azure call failed or no subscription is configured, not that none exist. It is a live Azure call per request. The companion GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/lan-side-connectivity/resourceGroupRegionVNetsMap is {resourceGroup: {region: [{id, name}]}}, keyed by region id, with the same null behaviour.

Reads a cache filled by a background poll (default every 4 hours); it never contacts Azure and has no freshness timestamp. An empty list means none discovered, never polled or cache wiped, never a 404. A stale list persists silently if Azure login fails or LAN-side orchestration is paused. routeServerName is derived from routeServerId.

Returns a map of vWAN id to a list of hub-id strings only; other hub properties are not exposed. It reads a cached snapshot written by the Azure LAN polling job, not Azure live. Before the first poll it returns {} at 200, which means not yet discovered and cannot be told apart from a subscription that has none. A parse failure on the stored snapshot is a plain-text 500.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/lanInterfa: Payload is a list of lists: [0] primary, [1] backup. LAN polling only uses it with exactly two groups and a non-empty group 0; other shapes read back fine but silently disable LAN orchestration. Unconfigured is [] at 200, not 404; deleting the Azure LAN subscription resets it. A row saved without an ids key makes every GET a 500 until a valid two-group value is re-POSTed.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/pauseOrche: Body carries paused (bool). true freezes orchestration (Azure polling returns early) without tearing down existing VWAN state. false is ambiguous: never configured looks the same as explicitly resumed. A corrupt or key-less stored row is a 500. This is a separate flag from the LAN-side pause. Changing it in either direction queues the whole appliance fleet for re-orchestration.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/subscripti: A bare 404 with empty body means no subscription is saved, not a fault. Always seven keys; clientSecret and storageAccountKey are always null, so you cannot tell whether they are set. Unknown stored keys are dropped. A 400 "Request is invalid - supply correct input" means a corrupt stored row, not your request.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/tunnelSett: When never saved, GET returns the Azure default, not null or 404, so it cannot be told from deliberately saved defaults (compare with GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/defaultTunnelSetting). Unset fields are omitted, so a missing key means null. The template is fleet-wide: a save queues a config push to every appliance.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/azure/virtualWan: Map is keyed vwanName to [nePk, ...], the opposite of its name. {} is a normal empty state. A key with an empty list is treated as absent. Orchestrator silently drops keys for VWANs that no longer exist when it refreshes from the subscription, so a read-back may differ from what was written.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/clearpass/accoun: Omit id for the map of all accounts (404 if none configured); with an integer id returns one (404 if the id is unknown). A 404 here means none or unknown, not a server fault.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/clearpass/events: startTime/endTime are epoch milliseconds, matched against session START only, so long-lived sessions begun before the window are missed; widen startTime. type is ALL|ACTIVE|HISTORICAL, uppercase; anything else returns 200 with an empty list. Newest first, so a small limit drops the oldest; limit=0 is empty. ip/username accept only leading/trailing *; % and _ act as wildcards.

type only matters as 'flow' (flow-derived tables); any other value or none reads login events. ip is required (400 'Invalid query parameters'). Setting both startTime and endTime to 0 drops the time filter and returns every username and role ever recorded for that IP.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/clearpass/pauseO: Returns {"pauseOrchestration":{"paused":bool}}. false is ambiguous: never configured and explicitly resumed look the same. A corrupt config row, or one lacking the paused key, is a 500, not a 4xx. A role without the ClearPass menu gets a bare 403.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/clearpass/servic: status is the last stored state, not live: context_server, login_context_server_action, logout_context_server_action as ints 0 CREATING, 1 CREATED, 2 AUTH_FAILED, 3 UNREACHABLE, 4 PAUSED, 5 FAILED; all 0 means never verified. Unknown id or empty stored credentials gives 400 "ClearPass Policy Manager account not exists for the given id".
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/applian: Empty config differs: Zscaler returns {"enabled":[]}, Netskope returns 200 with a null body if its cache is unpopulated. Rows in `enabled` hold nePk, priority, lastUpdateTime; priority is an election flag (1 eligible, 0 normal), not a rank, and with several 1s the winner is not deterministic. Duplicate nePks are not removed. Old data may list bare nePk strings; Zscaler omits null lastUpdateTime.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/connect: interfaceLabel is ignored; read the wanted key from the full map, keys are `<nePk>_<labelId>`. Empty nePk: zscaler 400, netskope 200 with an empty map (also empty if the appliance errored). Statuses are ambiguous: '1 of 2 Up' and 'Down' each have several causes (Down can mean both legs up with SLA disabled); 'Appliance Unreachable' also covers unknown nePk; 'Deleting' means not associated. Quote unrecognised strings verbatim.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/default: This is the factory-default tunnel setting used when an interface has no per-interface override.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/interfa: Object keyed by WAN interface label id. Netskope reads the cache only, so 200 with a bare null body means cache not populated, not unconfigured. With no stored row the first read builds and saves default settings for every current WAN label. presharedKey is returned in cleartext. Defaults differ by provider (Zscaler idType ufqdn, Netskope pfs true); Zscaler's default encryptionAlgorithm is the literal string null.

interfaces is a list of lists: [0] Primary, [1] Backup, [2] Secondary. Served from an in-process cache loaded at startup, so a change made behind Orchestrator shows only after restart. Unconfigured is interfaces [] with a defaulted tunnelSetting, not 404. A corrupt stored blob gives 200 with an empty body.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/ipslaRu: This is the IP-SLA probe template for the provider's passthrough tunnels. Zscaler is seeded at install with type http-monitor and a destination URL; Netskope is not seeded, so an empty 200 for netskope means not configured, not defaults. Unset fields are omitted, not null, so a missing key is not an explicit clear. enableIpslaRuleOrchestration exists for Zscaler only.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/ipslaSe: Single field `enableIpslaRuleOrchestration`; false means no IP-SLA rules are built for that provider's tunnels (tunnels unaffected). Defaults differ: an untouched zscaler reads false, an untouched netskope reads true because no row exists until the first write, so netskope true is ambiguous while false is definite.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/netskop: Requires READ_WRITE even though it is a GET. filter takes a NetskopeTaskApplianceStatus value.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/pauseOr: Reads an in-memory flag loaded at startup, not the database. paused:false is ambiguous: never configured, resumed, a torn-down zscaler subscription (resets to false), or on netskope an unparseable row; do not read it as running normally. After a POST the flag can stay stale if the cache refresh failed, so re-read to confirm.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/polling: Units are seconds (UI shows minutes); default 600 when never saved. Netskope returns {"pollingInterval": null} when its cache is not loaded (not unset) and 600 for a corrupt row; zscaler gives 500 for a corrupt row. Writes truncate to whole minutes, so a value not divisible by 60 does not match the real poll cadence.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/popOver: Map of nePk to labelId to {pop1, pop2}; keys are WAN interface-label ids, not names, and pop values may be an IPv4 address or an FQDN. {} is normal because only explicit overrides are listed. The map is not filtered by Appliance Access Group. During orchestration an override applies only if pop1 is non-empty. Entries are pruned when an appliance or label is removed.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/netskope/subscri: Both responses carry live credentials in the clear (netskope apiToken; zscaler partnerKey), so do not echo them. An error or 404 does not prove not subscribed: zscaler no-subscription is 404 {"message":"0-gzip"} (an ETag echo, not a reason), netskope is a 404 with empty body, and a zscaler 500 means a corrupt stored row. A narrow role may get zscaler data but 403 on netskope.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/serviceOrchestra: Returns {bioBreakout: 0|1} as an integer, not a boolean. When enabled, the provider's saved interface groups drive breakout policy, and a provider saved with only one group breaks orchestration. A blank or unknown serviceId is a 400 with the text in the body; a non-numeric serviceId gives a generic error.

serviceId must be the numeric provider id: unknown id gives a 500 with body "HTTP 400 Bad Request", non-numeric gives a 500 with parse text. interfaceLabel and remoteId are accepted but ignored. Unknown nePk is 200 with an empty list, same as an appliance with no tunnels. The echoed serviceId proves nothing.

Returns [[primary label ids], [backup label ids]], positional groups with no names. [] means never saved or saved with two empty groups. A one-group value is a latent fault, because breakout policy reads the second group. A blank or unknown serviceId is a 400; stored value that is not valid JSON is a 500.

For a provider never saved, ipslaSetting returns synthesized defaults (not stored; enableIpslaRuleOrchestration false) while ipslaRuleDestination is empty; treat that as nothing stored. Unset numeric fields are absent, not 0. Blank serviceId is 400; an unknown serviceId is 400 'Service Provider doesn't exists'; a non-numeric serviceId gives an opaque 500.

Server answers {"paused": bool}; any stored value other than 1 reads as false. Paused means Orchestrator stops reconciling this provider's tunnels; existing tunnels are left as they are. Blank serviceId is 400 'Invalid query parameters'; an unknown serviceId is 400 'Service Provider doesn't exists. Provide a valid Service Provider ID.'; a non-numeric serviceId gives a generic mapper error.

Response is inverted: {"<remoteEndpointId>":["<nePk>",...]}, keyed by endpoint id as a string; no associations is 200 {}. serviceId must be numeric: non-numeric is a 500, a numeric id with no provider is 400 "Service Provider doesn't exists". The matching write only reconciles endpoint ids present in the posted map, so posting {} changes nothing.

Any bad serviceId (unknown or non-numeric) returns a 500 whose body reads "HTTP 400 Bad Request"; only an empty serviceId is a real 400, so a 500 here usually means the id is wrong. Response is {"remoteEndpoints":[...]} (empty list if none) and includes plaintext preSharedKey values, so do not echo them. Unset strings come back empty, unset numbers as 0; row order is unspecified.

Pure database read: tunnelStatus is the last stored value and can be stale (Up, Down, 1 of 2 Up, Unknown, Appliance Unreachable, Pending). The appliance key is spelled nepk. An unknown serviceId gives a 500 with body 'HTTP 400 Bad Request', meaning no such provider; non-numeric serviceId is also 500. No rows gives 200 with []. Empty backupEndpointId means none; 0 ids may mean NULL.

Keys are strings ("7") though ids are integers, and order is arbitrary. {} means no service providers exist, not an error. Names are not unique, so key on the id. Any failure is one untyped 500 carrying the raw exception text.

Map key is <nePk>_<labelId>_<remoteEndpointId>. Empty identifier strings mean the tunnels are not in Orchestrator's in-memory cache (not orchestrated, unreachable, just restarted) or labelType was stored lowercase. Rows are silently skipped, so {} is ambiguous. Unknown serviceId is a 500 with body "HTTP 400 Bad Request"; non-numeric is a 500 with parse text.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/sse/connector: Always present: sseconMemSize, eligible and personaDetails {hasPersona, currentPersona, systemLimitsModified}. If no connector is installed, nepk, enabled, connectorName, connectorZone, status, details and installation are absent (not null), so test key presence. Every call is a live probe that pulls the install log from the appliance and is slow if it is unreachable. Unknown nePk is 400.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/sse/connector/st: Body is {nePk, status:{progress, isRunning, downloaded, installed}}; versions are strings, '' when unset, so empty installed means no connector. Status comes from the in-flight action, else the last completed job row, else the appliance; only the first is real-time, and the DB source always reports isRunning=false. Unknown nePk is 400, not 404.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/sse/connectorPoo: Effectively a single-row list (only region 0 is accepted). [] means either no pool or a swallowed failure; a malformed ipSupernet truncates the list with 200 and no error. `allocated` is a text string '<used>/<total>' (each connector interface uses 2 IPs; the global row also absorbs regions without a pool). segment, zone, role and label are ids, not names.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/sse/image: The image list is computed differently for container (cloud) and on-prem Orchestrators, chosen automatically. GET /thirdPartyServices/sse/image/refresh/status returns {refreshRequired, status} for the portal refresh.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/sse/interfaces: On the cached path a 404 'Appliance with key ... may be unreachable' is not evidence of reachability; for SSE it usually means no connector is installed yet. Retry with cached=false before concluding it is down. A successful live fetch is written back to the cache. An nePk Orchestrator does not know gives a bare 500, not 404.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/applianc: Empty config differs: Zscaler returns {"enabled":[]}, Netskope returns 200 with a null body if its cache is unpopulated. Rows in `enabled` hold nePk, priority, lastUpdateTime; priority is an election flag (1 eligible, 0 normal), not a rank, and with several 1s the winner is not deterministic. Duplicate nePks are not removed. Old data may list bare nePk strings; Zscaler omits null lastUpdateTime.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/connecti: interfaceLabel is ignored; read the wanted key from the full map, keys are `<nePk>_<labelId>`. Empty nePk: zscaler 400, netskope 200 with an empty map (also empty if the appliance errored). Statuses are ambiguous: '1 of 2 Up' and 'Down' each have several causes (Down can mean both legs up with SLA disabled); 'Appliance Unreachable' also covers unknown nePk; 'Deleting' means not associated. Quote unrecognised strings verbatim.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/countrie: The value is a raw plain-text string of pipe-delimited 'code, ENUM_NAME' pairs with a newline after each '|'; keep the newlines when round-tripping. An unset config is 204 No Content. If no countries row exists, this read persists the built-in default map into the config rows before returning it.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/defaultC: Value is a raw pipe-delimited string ("code, ENUM_NAME" pairs, each | followed by a newline), not parsed JSON. Empty is 204. If the defaultCountries row is absent this GET persists the built-in default, so a read can create config.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/defaultT: The body is a raw pipe-delimited string of 'Zone/Name, ENUM_NAME' pairs (each | followed by a newline), not parsed JSON; empty is 204. This GET can write: if the defaultTimezones row is absent it stores the built-in default before returning it. It omits the legacy aliases the configured list adds, so it can be a subset of that list.
This is the factory-default tunnel setting used when an interface has no per-interface override.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/interfac: Object keyed by WAN interface label id. Netskope reads the cache only, so 200 with a bare null body means cache not populated, not unconfigured. With no stored row the first read builds and saves default settings for every current WAN label. presharedKey is returned in cleartext. Defaults differ by provider (Zscaler idType ufqdn, Netskope pfs true); Zscaler's default encryptionAlgorithm is the literal string null.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/ipslaRul: This is the IP-SLA probe template for the provider's passthrough tunnels. Zscaler is seeded at install with type http-monitor and a destination URL; Netskope is not seeded, so an empty 200 for netskope means not configured, not defaults. Unset fields are omitted, not null, so a missing key is not an explicit clear. enableIpslaRuleOrchestration exists for Zscaler only.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/ipslaSet: Single field `enableIpslaRuleOrchestration`; false means no IP-SLA rules are built for that provider's tunnels (tunnels unaffected). Defaults differ: an untouched zscaler reads false, an untouched netskope reads true because no row exists until the first write, so netskope true is ambiguous while false is definite.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/location: invalidRule=true marks rules whose referenced appliance, group, region, label or zone no longer exists.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/orchestr: Returns {orchestrate: bool} from an in-memory cache, not the DB; if a save failed to persist, the cache still shows the saved value until restart. Never configured reads false, indistinguishable from an explicit false. Body is {orchestrate: bool}, read from cache. Never configured reads false, the same as an explicit false. If a save's persistence failed silently, the cache can show a value the database lacks until the next restart rebuilds it.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/pauseOrc: Reads an in-memory flag loaded at startup, not the database. paused:false is ambiguous: never configured, resumed, a torn-down zscaler subscription (resets to false), or on netskope an unparseable row; do not read it as running normally. After a POST the flag can stay stale if the cache refresh failed, so re-read to confirm.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/pollingI: Units are seconds (UI shows minutes); default 600 when never saved. Netskope returns {"pollingInterval": null} when its cache is not loaded (not unset) and 600 for a corrupt row; zscaler gives 500 for a corrupt row. Writes truncate to whole minutes, so a value not divisible by 60 does not match the real poll cadence.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/remoteEn: Whole fleet at once, no per-appliance read. Shape is {nePk: {labelId: {ip1, ip2}}}, where labelId is the WAN interface label id. Appliances whose stored value is {} are omitted, so an absent nePk means no overrides, not unknown appliance (there is no 404). One unparseable stored value makes the whole response a 500.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/subscrip: Both responses carry live credentials in the clear (netskope apiToken; zscaler partnerKey), so do not echo them. An error or 404 does not prove not subscribed: zscaler no-subscription is 404 {"message":"0-gzip"} (an ETag echo, not a reason), netskope is a 404 with empty body, and a zscaler 500 means a corrupt stored row. A narrow role may get zscaler data but 403 on netskope.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/timezone: timezones is a raw text string of pipe-delimited "Zone/Name, ENUM_NAME" pairs with a newline after each |, not JSON; keep the newlines when writing it back. Empty config is 204. If no row exists the first read persists the built-in default map and appends about 70 legacy aliases, so this GET writes config and returns a longer list.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/zdxVpnLo: Returns a map of nePk to a list of location and sub-location id/name pairs, used for ZDX correlation.
notes.GET /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/zscalerT: Requires READ_WRITE even though it is a GET. filter takes a ZscalerTaskApplianceStatus value.
notes.GET /trafficBehaviorMode: The mode governs how applications are steered (breakout vs backhaul). Omit nePk for the Orchestrator-wide mode, or pass it for one appliance.
notes.GET /tunnels2/bonded: Fabric-wide table served from the Orchestrator cache, not a live appliance read. overlayId only applies to /tunnels2/bonded. Omit nePk and tunnelId for the whole fabric and cap it with limit.
notes.GET /tunnels2/passThrough: Fabric-wide table served from the Orchestrator cache, not a live appliance read. overlayId only applies to /tunnels2/bonded. Omit nePk and tunnelId for the whole fabric and cap it with limit.
notes.GET /tunnels2/physical: Fabric-wide table served from the Orchestrator cache, not a live appliance read. overlayId only applies to /tunnels2/bonded. Omit nePk and tunnelId for the whole fabric and cap it with limit.
notes.GET /userAccount: Local accounts on the appliance, not Orchestrator users. cached=false writes the Orchestrator cache. cached=true with no stored row gives 404 'may be unreachable', which is only an empty cache; retry cached=false. Cached replays the last live fetch, so recent user changes appear only with cached=false. A bare 500 means unknown nePk or appliance dropped from cache; a hostname in the 500 means the live call failed.
notes.GET /users: The key is `userPk` (a string), not id. password, salt and userTwoFactorKey are always blanked to ""; use `passwordInit` (true = a password hash exists). `status` is 'Active' or 'Inactive' and `role` is 'Admin Manager' (net_read_write) or 'Network Monitor' (net_read); null means an unmapped row. `expireTime` is the password expiry in epoch ms, 0 = never. userId is matched against the username.
notes.GET /users/validateCommonwords: Returns a bare boolean: true means the lowercased password is in the common-word blocklist and would be rejected; false only means it passes this one check.
notes.GET /virtualif/loopback: Response is a map keyed by interface name (lo1, vti0), {} when none; label, zone, role/role_id and vrf_id are IDs, not names. VTI behindNAT is auto, none, or the literal public IP. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" means no cached row yet; retry cached=false, which also refreshes the cache. Unknown nePk is a 500, blank is 400; only lowercase true uses the cache.
notes.GET /virtualif/vti: Response is a map keyed by interface name (lo1, vti0), {} when none; label, zone, role/role_id and vrf_id are IDs, not names. VTI behindNAT is auto, none, or the literal public IP. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" means no cached row yet; retry cached=false, which also refreshes the cache. Unknown nePk is a 500, blank is 400; only lowercase true uses the cache.
notes.GET /vrf/config/enable: enable defaults to false if never written (no 404). Segments map is keyed by segment id as a string; segment "0" Default is synthesized into every response, so a one-entry map means no user segments. Deleted segments are not returned (status is always 0). Ids 1-65400 are reused after deletion. Segments can exist while enable is false; disabling is rejected while non-default segments remain.
notes.GET /vrf/config/maps: Swagger describes inter-segment DNAT policies; HPE describes inter-segment routing maps that define how traffic routes or leaks from a source segment to destination segments.
notes.GET /vrf/config/securityPoliciesSegments: The list holds only segment-pair keys (sourceSegmentId_destinationSegmentId) that have a saved policy row, not all existing pairs. A pair missing from the list is not proven unfiltered.
notes.GET /vrf/config/segments: enable defaults to false if never written (no 404). Segments map is keyed by segment id as a string; segment "0" Default is synthesized into every response, so a one-entry map means no user segments. Deleted segments are not returned (status is always 0). Ids 1-65400 are reused after deletion. Segments can exist while enable is false; disabling is rejected while non-default segments remain.
notes.GET /vrf/config/snatMaps: One Orchestrator-wide map, not per appliance; {} when unset. Keys are "<srcSegmentId>_<dstSegmentId>"; values are {enable, gms_marked, comment}. gms_marked separates Orchestrator-owned rules from ones configured locally on an appliance.
notes.GET /vrfSegments: Same data as GET /dnatMaps (shared cache row of appliance resource /vrf/config/maps, byte-identical); cached=false here overwrites what a cached read of either returns. Not the Orchestrator-wide /vrf/config/maps. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" only means nothing cached yet; retry cached=false. Unknown nePk is an opaque 500.
notes.GET /vrrp: Raw passthrough of the appliance's JSON; fields are not validated. cached must be exactly lowercase true/false; other spellings (TRUE, 1) silently take the live path. cached=true 404 "may be unreachable" means never cached, not unreachable; retry cached=false. A successful live read overwrites the cache. Blank nePk is 400 "Invalid nePk"; unknown nePk is an opaque 500.
notes.GET /vxoaImages: Entries use dotted keys (NxImage.fileName, NxImage.version, NxImage.buildDate, NxImage.lastModified in epoch ms) plus portalDownloaded, which only means the name matches pdimage-*. This GET can delete a writable image file that fails to open as corrupt. refreshStatus.status is INITIAL, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED or FAILED and is global to the Orchestrator.
notes.GET /wccp/config/group: Each WCCP path (group, system, state) reads a separate cache row, so one nePk can succeed on one and 404 on another; a 404 "Appliance with key ... may be unreachable" only means not cached yet, so retry cached=false. A 200 can carry prose such as "WCCP is not enabled" instead of JSON config. A 500 "internal server error" can mean an empty cached row. cached=false writes the cache.
notes.GET /zones: zones is a map keyed by zone-id string with only a name; no saved zones is {} with 200. nextId is {"nextId":n}, a per-request suggestion that reserves nothing (concurrent callers get the same id); ceiling is 65400 with VRF, 135 without. allVRFZones=true is a separate path that can silently drop zones and merges same ids across segments, so a short result proves nothing.
notes.GET /zones/eeEnable: Returns {"eeEnable":{"enable":bool}}; a never-written config reads false at 200, no 404. Factory default is true, so false usually means someone turned it off. true is Orchestrator intent only: appliances can lag and appliances below 9.0.0.0_0000 never receive it. Enabling routing segmentation turns it on.
notes.GET /zones/nextId: zones is a map keyed by zone-id string with only a name; no saved zones is {} with 200. nextId is {"nextId":n}, a per-request suggestion that reserves nothing (concurrent callers get the same id); ceiling is 65400 with VRF, 135 without. allVRFZones=true is a separate path that can silently drop zones and merges same ids across segments, so a short result proves nothing.
notes.GET /zones/vrfZonesMap: Nested map: segment id, then zone INDEX (not the zone id), then {id,name}. Zone index 255 (Unknown) is stripped. A missing config row gives {} rather than 404. Related /zones/vrfSegmentZonesMap is a flat list of {zoneId, zoneName, vrfId, vrfName} without the index, and it can 500 if the zone map references a deleted segment.
notes.POST /alarm/appliance: view is active|closed|all; anything else is a generic 400. maxAlarms (default 1000, 1-100000) is one SQL LIMIT shared across all nePks, so raise it before concluding there are none. orderBySeverity affects only active; closed sorts by close time and all by id desc, so truncation keeps the most recent. Closed/all rows add cleared fields. Body without nePks is 404, empty list 400; out-of-group nePks are silently stripped (403 if none remain).
notes.POST /alarm/delayEmail: When the delay is nonzero the notifier scans back duration*2 seconds but never less than 10 minutes, so any nonzero duration below 300 seconds gives the same 10-minute look-back; raising it from 10s to 60s does not widen the scan.
notes.POST /applicationDefinition/applicationT: pattern is required (400 otherwise) and is a Java regex matched case-insensitively as a substring, not a glob; a bare '*' does not mean everything, and an invalid regex gives 400. limit defaults to 30 (0 means 30). Truncation takes the first N matches in internal order and only then sorts, so an exact match can be missing; raise limit before concluding a name does not exist.
notes.POST /applicationDefinition/applications: pattern is a Java regex matched case-insensitively as a substring, not a glob (a bare * misbehaves; invalid regex gives 400). limit defaults to 30 (0 becomes 30) and you get the best-ranked N (pattern-prefix first), not the first N. pattern is required unless AVC mode is none (400 'please specify the pattern for search'); with AVC mode none, pattern and limit are ignored and all applications return.
notes.POST /brandCustomization: The six text types are footer, welcomeText, patentText, orchText, supportLinkURL and homePageTitle. Image branding is separate.
notes.POST /edge-ha/groups: An HAGroup carries its appliance members plus the HA subnet, mask and vlanStart, and IPv6 HA subnet settings.
notes.POST /gms/appliance/preconfiguration/fin: Body keys are serial (not serialNum) and tag; at least one is required. They are ORed, not ANDed, and matched with SQL LIKE, so % and _ are wildcards and only one arbitrary match is returned. A miss is a bare 404 with no body. configData in the match is base64-encoded; decode it before reading the preconfig YAML.
notes.POST /gms/discovery: Body example: {"emails":["a@b.com"],"secondaryAccounts":{"acctName":["c@d.com"]}}; secondaryAccounts maps an account name to its list of emails.
notes.POST /gms/job/reportViewport: Map keys are chart display names (e.g. Health Map, Loss, Jitter Trends, Top Talkers), matched case-insensitively, not internal tab ids. A map keyed by ids is stored without error but silently does nothing.
notes.POST /gms/vti/cidr: vtiSettings is {ipAddress, mask}, the pool definition only. The individual /30 subnets carved from it are held separately as reservedSubnets.
notes.POST /gms/wizard: The only modelled field is `autoOpen` (bool): whether the getting-started wizard opens on login. The UI sets it to false once the wizard is dismissed.
notes.POST /gmsLicense/aas/token/validate: Body is {feature:{"value":[N]}}; pass the bare feature name ("boost" is checked against boostLimit). A feature is only checked if value is a non-empty list whose first element is a number; others are silently dropped, so confirm every key you sent comes back (missing means not checked, not fits). Only the first list element is validated. Nothing is persisted; empty body is 400.
notes.POST /gmsLicense/aas/token/validate/hub: Body maps an appliance key (nePk or any placeholder) to {site, networkRole, regionId}, the role/region you intend to apply; omitted fields inherit the appliance's current values. 200 {"validation":{}} is a PASS; a failure is 200 with validation.message, and only the first offending region is reported. Only HUB and NRHUB roles count. An empty body also returns a pass, so send at least one entry. Persists nothing.
notes.POST /health: Body {from,to,nePks,overlayId,verticals}; from/to are epoch seconds (ms silently returns empty). overlayId must be an integer: 0 underlay, -1 all overlays, n one overlay. verticals must be non-empty (empty returns nothing): ALARM, LOSS, LATENCY, BW_UTILIZATION, CONFIG, REBOOT, JITTER, MOS. Response is padded with blank rows (blank:true, status null = no data, not healthy); any bad field gives the same opaque 400.
notes.POST /loopbackOrch: Body is a map whose top-level keys are segment ids as strings. Per segment: loopbackPool (subnet string like "10.0.0.0/24"), interfaces (interface id to {mgmtIp,label,zone,role_id}) and regionSettings (region id to the same three fields, or null when no per-region overrides). Regions appear only nested under a segment.
notes.POST /modelSpec: Read-only despite POST. Body fields: models (modelName, optional partNum) and searchKeys. Result is {modelSpec:{key:spec}}, key modelName_partNum or modelName, HTML-escaped (EC&V becomes EC&V). Unknown model gives null/absent keys; entries without modelName are skipped. Each call narrows the cached spec to the requested searchKeys (searchKeys [""] empties it).
notes.POST /modelSpec/portList: Response keys are HTML-escaped (send 'EC&V', look under 'EC&V') and the value is null for a model that could not be resolved. A body like models [{}] or an empty modelName returns 200 with an empty map, not an error. The backend forces searchKeys to spec.networking.ports, which narrows the cached spec of those models to ports only, so later /modelSpec reads for other keys go back to the portal.
notes.POST /orch-ha/reachability: customDefaultReachability maps each HA instance id to the IP or DNS name the other instances should use to reach it. The optional reachabilityForLabel overrides that default per interface label, each entry carrying a labelId and a priority.
notes.POST /portProfiles/config: Each element is {id, name, config}; config holds sysConfig, mgmtIfData, modeIfs, dpRoutes and dhcpFailover. Profiles are reusable interface-label/port layouts applied to appliances during deployment.
notes.POST /realtimeStats: nePk is a query param; the body is the appliance's own query {type,name,filter}, forwarded verbatim and not validated (types include tunnel, interface, shaper, flow, dscp, ipsla, trafficType, ddos, drops; never 'app'). Reply timestamps are in NANOSECONDS. An unknown nePk gives a bare 500; an unreachable appliance or rejected query gives 500 '<hostname>: Failed to get realtime stats from appliance.', not a 400.
notes.POST /security/endEntityProfiles: label is the primary key; the 32-profile cap and duplicate-label check apply on create only. csr_attrs is a four-part underscore string like rsa_2048_with_sha256, checked on create against the active cipher profile. purpose (sd_wan|tls_server|tls_client|general) is unvalidated; tunnels use only general and sd_wan. Apply is deferred per appliance; changes to purpose, global_san_email_domain, subject_use_serial, gms_marked push nothing.
notes.POST /spPortal/ztp: Only field is enableManualProvisioning: true means new appliances must supply an account key instead of being approved automatically. Orchestrator mirrors it to the cloud portal, where it is named requireAccountKey.
notes.POST /stats/aggregate/application2: Swagger says startTime/endTime are ms; HPE reports epoch seconds. Body is {"nePks":[...]}. An empty window with lastHour=true is silently re-run one hour earlier; check MIN_TIMESTAMP/MAX_TIMESTAMP. Hourly data only. `top` can return top+1 rows, ranked by LAN bytes. groupByNE defaults true (one row per app per appliance). Unknown application gives []; unknown nePk fails the call.
notes.POST /stats/aggregate/boost: Body is {"nePks":["1.NE"]}. granularity: minute, hour or day only (month is accepted but has no table). groupByNE=false collapses to one fleet-wide row without nePk; appliances with no data are simply absent, which does not prove unlicensed. Response is an array in unstable order; `boost` is a count of intervals, not bytes; `configured` is peak Kbps. Default retention: 3 days (minute), 14 days (hour); older data is silently missing.
notes.POST /stats/aggregate/securityPolicy: Body is {"nePks":[...]}. HPE reports granularity words are minute, hour, day (month has no table); Swagger lists hourly/daily/monthly. `top` is ignored and every zone pair returns. groupByNE=false sums the fleet per fromZone/toZone. Zones are opaque IDs; routing_drop_* is a routing fault, not a policy deny. [] means no data.
notes.POST /stats/aggregate/topTalkers: Body is {"nePks":[...]}. Response is a list of single-key maps {nePk:[rows]}; a failed appliance is silently absent. With lastHour=true an empty window is silently re-run one hour earlier, so check MIN_TIME/MAX_TIME. `top` is per appliance by LAN bytes; splitByNe does nothing. Rows are per source only: DEST_* blank, FLOW_COUNT null, empty SOURCE_IP becomes "Others".
notes.POST /stats/aggregate/tunnel: Swagger says startTime/endTime are ms; HPE reports epoch seconds, window half-open [startTime,endTime). Body is {"nePks":[...]}. overlay 'all' means bonded overlays only (underlay excluded), '0' means physical only. top is a network-wide limit after ranking, not per appliance; a negative top 500s. granularity month 500s. Ranking is worst-first only for loss, latency, jitter (desc) and mos (asc); other metrics rank best first.
notes.POST /stats/config/applianceBusinessHour: Body is {"nePks":[...]}. Result {businessHours:[...]} has nePk, iscustombusinesshour, businesshourstart, businesshourend, timezone (lowercase except nePk). Only explicitly configured appliances appear, so [] is valid; match by nePk. Every error (unknown nePk, null body, missing nePks) is a 500 'Failed to get ApplianceBusinessHourConfig properties'. timezone is always a concrete zone id.
notes.POST /stats/config/availabilityThreshold: The API sections are overlayAvailability, underlayAvailability, networkRoleAvailability, interfaceAvailability and reachability. The UI relabels two: its "service" availability is overlayAvailability and its "transport" availability is underlayAvailability.
notes.POST /stats2/aggregate/apdex: Body is {"nePks":[...]}, not an array of {nePk} (that 400s). timestamp is epoch seconds, a lower bound with no upper bound; omitting it is not 'latest', so pass one (e.g. now-3600); data is kept 3 days. Rows with timestamp -1 or apdex -1 are no-data placeholders; currentBestPath holds the path name; empty data usually means no AppExpress groups.
notes.POST /stats2/aggregate/applicationPerfor: Body must be {"nePks":[...]}, not an array. Response is {column_def,data} with positional rows, and positions 3 and 4 are swapped: row[3] is really client network delay and row[4] server delay. Delays are average ms truncated to whole ms, so 0 does not mean no data; apps with no samples are absent. limit applies after sorting by nePk (not per appliance) and is capped at 10000. Use granularity minute, hour or day only.
notes.POST /stats2/aggregate/dns: Body is a JSON array of {"nePk":...}, not {nePks}. Response is per-appliance maps of bare value arrays plus a trailing "header" entry; zip header[0] by name (order is not fixed; domain is CALC_DNS). top is per appliance (up to top+1 rows). A failed appliance is silently absent. groupBySubDomains must be 1-4; only groupBy=COUNTRY works. Data is hourly, so windows under 1h can match nothing.
notes.POST /stats2/aggregate/interfaceOverlay: Body is only [{"nePk": ...}]; time window, granularity and overlay go in the query. granularity is minute|hour|day; month passes validation but has no table and returns an empty 200. Failed appliances (or a down stats DB) are silently dropped, so compare nePks sent vs returned. Rows are bare arrays: zip with the trailing "header" entry. A just-started window can be empty; MAX_OHEAD_RX_BYTES_MAX always repeats the TX value.
notes.POST /stats2/aggregate/ports: Body is a JSON array [{"nePk":"..."}], not {nePks}. Response is [{nePk:[[values]]}, ..., {"header":[[names]]}]; map columns by header name, not position (COUNT is always 0). A failed appliance is silently absent, so compare keys with the nePks sent. `top` is per appliance, ranked by LAN bytes. Data is hourly, so windows under an hour can match nothing.
notes.POST /stats2/aggregate/user2: Body is {"nePks":[...]}, not an array. Response is single-key maps per nePk plus a trailing 'header' entry (column names; zip by name); the nePk column in rows is always empty. Rows include a synthetic __total__ user, so do not sum rows. top is per appliance and can return top+1 rows. Failed appliances are silently absent; data is hourly, so windows under an hour may match nothing.
notes.POST /statsCollector/associationsByNepks: Every nePk must exist and have a collector assigned: one unassigned or unknown nePk makes the whole call 400 'Request is invalid - supply correct input', with no partial map. An empty nePks list is 404 with no body. With an Appliance Access Group, out-of-group ids are silently dropped; if all are dropped you get 403.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/awstgnm/tunnelS: mode follows the label type in the factory profile: ipsec for WAN labels and gre for LAN labels, and only active interface labels get a profile.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/axis/locations: Body is a bare JSON list of nePks; a wrongly shaped body gives a bare 500. The result is a flat list with one row per appliance and WAN label, so group by nepk plus labelId; appliances with no tunnel config or an unknown nePk simply vanish. Missing values are "" not null. `popIps` is one comma-joined string resolved from the appliance's cached nslookup table, so an empty half means not in that cache.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/netskope/ipslaR: This is the probe template Orchestrator stamps onto every IP-SLA rule it builds for Netskope passthrough tunnels: type, destination, routeLabelId, sourceInterface, plus the timing and threshold fields (keepAliveInterval, interval, samplingWindow, httpTimeout, up/down thresholds, up/down loss and latency, metricCombination).
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/netskope/ipslaS: The object has exactly one field, `enableIpslaRuleOrchestration`. When false, Orchestrator builds no IP-SLA monitoring rules for the provider's passthrough tunnels; the tunnels themselves are unaffected.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/netskope/orches: Body is a bare JSON array of nePks (not {nePks:[...]}); a non-array is 400, an empty body is 500. Unknown nePks are simply absent, so match results by `nepk`. Config fields are JSON strings needing a second parse ('{}' when unset). Preshared key comes back as "" (redacted, not unconfigured). Zscaler only: up/dnBandwidth are in Mbps (0 = control off, -1 = inherit) and idle/surrogate times are in the sibling unit field's unit, not minutes.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/ipslaRu: These fields form the probe template stamped onto every IP-SLA rule Orchestrator builds for the provider's passthrough tunnels: type, destination, routeLabelId, sourceInterface, keepAliveInterval, interval, samplingWindow, up/down thresholds, loss and latency, httpTimeout, metricCombination. enableIpslaRuleOrchestration is Zscaler-only.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/ipslaSe: The object has exactly one field, enableIpslaRuleOrchestration. When false, Orchestrator builds no IP-SLA monitoring rules for the provider's passthrough tunnels; the tunnels themselves are unaffected.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/locatio: Each rule maps appliances/groups/regions plus WAN labels and LAN sub-locations to a Zscaler location. The backend sets invalidRule=true on rules whose referenced appliance, group, region, label or zone no longer exists.
notes.POST /thirdPartyServices/zscaler/orchest: Body is a bare JSON array of nePks (not {nePks:[...]}); a non-array is 400, an empty body is 500. Unknown nePks are simply absent, so match results by `nepk`. Config fields are JSON strings needing a second parse ('{}' when unset). Preshared key comes back as "" (redacted, not unconfigured). Zscaler only: up/dnBandwidth are in Mbps (0 = control off, -1 = inherit) and idle/surrogate times are in the sibling unit field's unit, not minutes.
notes.POST /tunnels/bonded/config/getBatch: Body is a bare JSON list of tunnel ids, not an object. With cached=true the result is a map {tunnelId: {...}} and ids with no stored row are silently dropped, so a short or empty map is not an error; cached=false proxies to the appliance and an unreachable appliance is a 500 'Failed to get tunnels'. Third-party tunnels use the name passThrough in these paths.

notes.POST /tunnels/physical/tracerouteState: Body is {"nePks":["<nePk>"]}; physical tunnels only. An empty {} 200 means no result yet or a swallowed read failure, so do not poll forever. Appliance HTTP errors pass through with their status but the generic message 'There was an internal server error.'; an unknown tunnel id and an unknown nePk both give that same 500, so verify both beforehand.
notes.POST /tunnels2/getTunnelsBetweenApplianc: Served from Orchestrator caches; no appliance is contacted. Body is {"nePks":[...]} and the same list is source and destination, so it finds tunnels among those appliances (one nePk yields only self-tunnels). overlayId empty or '0' disables bonded tunnels and is the only case where includePassThrough has effect; any other value enables bonded. Use 'all' or a numeric id; other text gives a bare 500.
notes.POST /tunnels2/tunnelCounts: Counts only, no up/down state, taken from Orchestrator's synced tunnel2 table, so they lag the appliances by one sync cycle. Body is only {"nePks":[...]}; there is no cached param. Result is nePk -> {Underlay, Passthrough, Total, plus one key per overlay name}; a missing key means zero. An empty nePks body returns 204 with no content.
notes.POST /validateApplianceUpgrade: GET cached 404 'Failed to get data from GMS Cache' means not polled yet; use cached=false (on connection failure it returns 200 with the text 'REST API call to /appliancesSoftwareVersions failed!'). POST /validateApplianceUpgrade takes {nePks}, needs READ_WRITE, silently drops unknown nePks (all unknown validates every appliance), and returns a sentence in Air-Gap mode; errors usually come from the Cloud Portal.
notes.POST /vrf/config/enable: enable and the segments are independent config rows: segments can exist while enable is false. Disabling is what couples them; it is rejected while any non-default segment remains.
notes.POST /zones/nextId: Body is the object {"nextId": <int>}, not a bare integer.
notes.PUT /alarm/delayEmail: When duration is nonzero the notifier scans back duration * 2 seconds but never less than 10 minutes, so any nonzero value below 300 seconds gives the same 10-minute look-back window.
notes.PUT /portProfiles/config: Each profile is {id, name, config}; config holds sysConfig, mgmtIfData, modeIfs, dpRoutes and dhcpFailover.
notes.PUT /security/cipherProfile: A profile has id, profile (the name), active, editable, comments, plus sub-objects tls, tunnel, ssh, certificate, snmp, ntp and cluster whose wire names differ from their UI labels.
notes.PUT /security/endEntityProfiles: Apply is deferred and per appliance. Changing only purpose, global_san_email_domain, subject_use_serial or gms_marked stores the value but pushes nothing. Update validates nothing (only create checks the 32-profile cap, case-insensitive duplicate label and csr_attrs), so illegal values can be stored. label is the key, matched exactly. csr_attrs looks like rsa_2048_with_sha256. purpose is unvalidated: sd_wan, tls_server, tls_client, general.

appliance_rest_urls.userApps: Returns the string "{}" rather than an object when there are no user apps.
appliance_rest_urls.interfaceLabels/lan: Flat {id: name} map of LAN labels only.
appliance_rest_urls.interfaceLabels: Live read of the appliance's own labels as {"lan":{id:name},"wan":{id:name}}, flat id-to-name maps. The Orchestrator-wide label registry differs (values are objects with name and active); a mismatch between the two usually means a label push is still pending. No cached option.
appliance_rest_urls.sslSubstituteCert: builtin_signing true means the factory certificate; cert-substitution false means no TLS substitution. The fingerprint differs per appliance even on the factory certificate.
appliance_rest_urls.flowRedirection/state: An empty list is normal for a non-clustered appliance. Counters are cumulative since boot: poll twice and divide the deltas by timeStamp (epoch ms).
appliance_rest_urls.networkRoutes: Management-plane routing table, not the SD-WAN data path. mgmt rows with dynamic:true are learned and read-only; only dynamic:false rows are static. lan may be empty.
appliance_rest_urls.stats/drops/meta/info: About 400 numeric-string codes mapped to drop reasons. Constant per software release, so fetch once from any appliance and again after an upgrade.
appliance_rest_urls.subnets/state/peersInfo: [] is normal when subnet sharing is unused or not yet converged; 404 means the appliance software is too old. txsecs/rxsecs are seconds since the last tx/rx.
appliance_rest_urls.lte/detailData: {} means no modem or unsupported (normal). Otherwise one entry per interface (e.g. cell0) with config and state; plugged_in false means no modem; rssi is a string such as -75dBm.
appliance_rest_urls.idsips/stats: Buckets keyed by epoch ms, unordered; negative values mean no data; kernel_drops and flow_drop_count are cumulative. The &from value is epoch ms.
appliance_rest_urls.poe/config: 404 "no poe interfaces found" means the appliance has no PoE hardware. power_mode is 0-5; priority is honoured only at power_mode 3 or higher.
appliance_rest_urls.poe/state: 404 "no poe interfaces found" means the appliance has no PoE hardware.
appliance_rest_urls.poe/state/system: A 500 wrapping an appliance 404 "no bindings ... sys_stats" means no PoE hardware, not a fault. Check the appliance scalars for a non-empty poeInterfaces first.
appliance_rest_urls.sysLimits: Entries are objects; the effective limit is the value field. steps is the selectable ladder (memory in MiB), not the limit. limitsLocked is a bare boolean.
appliance_rest_urls.ipAllowList: The appliance's own inbound allow-list, not the Orchestrator's. The ip key is omitted when there are no rules; check enable too, since rules are not enforced when it is false. Older software lacks this url.
appliance_rest_urls.cloudApplications/config: rtt_interval is in seconds, rtt_threshold in ms; a missing client_enabled or ssl_enabled means false. The application list rebuilds asynchronously after an enable change, so read again.
appliance_rest_urls.cachedRole: Rows are under data in {matched, data}; matched 0 is normal. Wrongly spelled filters (maxRows, ipAddress, segment, macAddress, effectiveRole) are silently ignored.
appliance_rest_urls.powerSupply: 404 "No Power Supply Info found" means a virtual appliance. powr is watts; power_supply_type 1 means dual supplies (read ps1/ps2), 0 a single one (read the top-level voltage/current).
appliance_rest_urls.tunnelAliases: Bare list of {id, alias}; empty is normal. Only named tunnels are listed, so built-in pseudo tunnels are missing.
appliance_rest_urls.bondedTunnels/aliases: Bare list of {id, alias}; empty is normal.
appliance_rest_urls.thirdPartyTunnels/aliases: Bare list of {id, alias}; empty is normal.
appliance_rest_urls.memory: KiB counters: total, free, buffers, cached, used, swapTotal, swapFree, swapUsed. buffers and cached are reclaimable, so used minus cached is the real memory pressure.
appliance_rest_urls.overlays3/config: The overlays a route policy may choose from; values not listed here are rejected. The path varies by build: overlays3, overlays2 or overlays.
appliance_rest_urls.peers: The peers a route policy may choose from; values not listed here are rejected.
appliance_rest_urls.interfaces/routeMapPreferredPath: The preferred-path interfaces a route policy may choose from; values not listed here are rejected.
appliance_rest_urls.hwdebug: Needs a command (ethtool, lscpu, lshw, dmidecode, lsusb or lspci; case-sensitive), otherwise 400. Only ethtool output is structured, and it is flaky: empty means retry, not no NICs.
appliance_rest_urls.security/ddos/protectionProfile/{zoneId}: Replace {zoneId} with the numeric zone id. {} means no profile mapped or an unknown zone id (not validated); no stats_export key means unsupported software; false means stats are off; true means ready.
appliance_rest_urls.nexthops: nhop_state is reachable or unreachable; nhop_uptime is milliseconds in the current state (not an epoch); source is WAN or LAN. An empty list means no next hops are tracked.
appliance_rest_urls.security/ddos/ipReputation: One nePk, read live; needs the adv_sec licence and software 9.6.0.0 or later. Capped at the 50 most recent hosts, so a missing host proves nothing. state is lowercase, timestamp is epoch seconds (as a string), zoneId is numeric.
